INTRODUCTION

介绍

# ↩

You Should Read This Book If Your Organization Needs Revenues

如果你的组织需要收入，你应该读这本书

A merican Indian tradition exalts the Rainmaker. The Rainmaker used magical powers to bring the rain to nourish the crops to feed the people. Without the rain, the people would weaken, die, or have to move elsewhere.

美国印第安人的传统崇敬祈雨神。祈雨神运用神奇的力量带来雨水，滋润庄稼，养活人民。没有雨水，人们就会衰弱、死亡，或者不得不迁徙。

Today, a Rainmaker is a person who brings revenue into an organization, be it profit or not-for-profit. That revenue comes from customers and donors. That revenue is the aqua viva —the lifeblood—of the organization. Without it the organization will die.

如今，“造雨人”指的是为组织（无论盈利还是非盈利）带来收入的人。这些收入来自顾客和捐赠者。这些收入是组织的“生命之水”（aqua viva），也就是命脉。没有它，组织就会消亡。

Customers’ money is the rain.

顾客的钱就是雨水。

The term Rainmaker is more commonly used in such professional service industries as legal, accounting, consulting, investment banking, advertising, and architecture. In these industries, Rainmakers are the two or so people in the firm who are responsible for generating most of the new customers, the new business.

“造雨人”一词在法律、会计、咨询、投资银行、广告和建筑等专业服务行业更为常见。在这些行业中，“造雨人”指的是公司中负责开发大部分新客户（即新业务）的两名左右的人员。

Big-hitting Rainmakers are among the highest paid employees in every company in every industry. They operate under many titles: owner, partner, chancellor, sales representative, CEO, agent, managing director, and fund-raiser. If becoming a Rainmaker is your goal, then this book will help you get there.

各行各业中，每家公司里收入最高的员工都属于“雨人”。他们拥有各种头衔：老板、合伙人、总经理、销售代表、首席执行官、经纪人、总经理以及筹款人。如果您的目标是成为一名“雨人”，那么这本书将助您一臂之力。

There is another kind of Rainmaker, and he or she is an employee—or associate or colleague or team member or crew member. Every employee must be somehow involved in the identification, attraction, getting, and keeping of customers. The advice in this book tilts to the salesperson, but if you have contact with customers, or work with and support colleagues who have contact with customers, this book will make you more effective. You will be better able to sell inside, to sell your ideas to your organization.

还有另一种“雨人”，他或她是员工——或者同事、同事、团队成员或工作人员。每位员工都必须以某种方式参与识别、吸引、获取和留住客户。本书的建议主要针对销售人员，但如果你与客户有联系，或者与接触客户的同事共事并提供支持，本书将帮助你提高效率。你将能够更好地进行内部销售，更好地向你的组织推销你的想法。

The most important success factor in any business or organization is having a customer. This is more important than the business idea, the products, the machinery, the buildings, the financing, or the people. It is customer money that pays everyone’s salary, that pays for 401(k) plans, union dues, bonuses, vacations, health insurance, computers, and office furniture. Customers are known by many names: members, students, fans, soldiers, parishioners, and patients. Regardless of what they are called, without customers no organization can continue to survive.

任何企业或组织最重要的成功因素是拥有客户。这比商业理念、产品、机器、建筑、融资或人员都更重要。客户的钱支付着每个人的薪水，支付着401(k)计划、工会会费、奖金、假期、医疗保险、电脑和办公家具的费用。客户有很多种称呼：会员、学生、粉丝、士兵、教区居民和病人。无论他们被称为什么，没有客户，任何组织都无法生存。

Therefore, the paramount job of every single employee in an organization is to, directly or indirectly, get and keep customers. This is true without exception!

因此，组织中每位员工的首要任务就是直接或间接地获取并留住客户。这一点毋庸置疑！

The job of every employee is to help ring the cash register. The job of every employee is to keep the customers coming, and to keep the customers coming back.

每个员工的职责就是帮忙敲收银机。每个员工的职责就是吸引顾客，并让顾客再次光临。

This book is a recipe for how to sell, for how to make rain, be it drizzle or deluge, sprinkle or storm. If your organization needs revenues, and if you want to become invaluable to your organization, then read this book.

这本书是一本关于如何销售的秘诀，教你如何催生雨水——无论是毛毛细雨还是倾盆大雨，无论是细雨还是暴风雨。如果你的组织需要收入，并且希望成为组织中不可或缺的人物，那么请阅读这本书。

The Rainmaker’s Credo

雨人信条

• Cherish customers at all times.

• 时刻珍惜客户。

• Treat customers as you would your best friend.

• 像对待最好的朋友一样对待客户。

• Listen to customers and decipher their needs.

• 倾听客户的意见并了解他们的需求。

• Make (or give) customers what they need.

• 制造（或给予）顾客他们所需要的东西。

• Price your product to its dollarized value.

• 根据产品的美元价值为其定价。

• Show customers the dollarized value of what they will get.

• 向顾客展示他们将获得的产品的美元价值。

• Teach customers to want what they need.

• 教导顾客了解他们所需要的东西。

• Make your product the way customers want it.

• 按照客户的需求生产产品。

• Get your product to your customers when they want it.

• 在客户需要时将产品送达他们。

• Give your customers a little extra, more than they expect.

• 为您的客户提供超出他们预期的额外服务。

• Remind customers of the dollarized value they received.

• 提醒顾客他们收到的美元价值。

• Thank each customer sincerely and often.

• 经常真诚地感谢每位顾客。

• Help customers pay you, so they won’t be embarrassed and go elsewhere.

• 帮助客户向您付款，这样他们就不会感到尴尬而去其他地方付款。

• Ask to do it again.

• 要求再做一次。

• 2 •

• 2 •

Always Answer the Question “Why Should This Customer Do Business with Us?”

始终回答“为什么这个客户应该与我们做生意？”这个问题

N ever make a sales call on a customer unless you can answer the question “Why should this customer do business with our company, with me?” The answer must be a benefit to the customer. The answer must fit the customer’s agenda, not yours. The customer should do business with you because you will make him feel good, or you will solve his problem, or both. There must be a business benefit and a personal benefit—often interlinked—for the customer. For example, a business benefit might be getting a new product to market sooner, thereby generating millions of dollars in new sales. The personal benefit might be a job promotion for the customer.

除非你能回答“为什么这个客户应该与我们公司、与我公司做生意？”这个问题，否则千万不要主动拜访客户。答案必须对客户有利。答案必须符合客户的意愿，而不是你的。客户应该与你做生意，是因为你会让他感觉良好，或者你会解决他的问题，或者两者兼而有之。对客户来说，必须有商业利益和个人利益——通常是相互关联的。例如，商业利益可能是更快地将新产品推向市场，从而创造数百万美元的新销售额。个人利益可能是客户的职位晋升。

If the benefit makes the customer feel good, then, for example, the effective furnace or natural gas salesperson’s answer might be “The customer will get warm, cozy rooms.” (The ineffective furnace salesperson thinks the customer is buying BTUs.) If your product solves a problem then the answer to the question should be phrased in dollars and cents. For example, assume a software program enables a hotel to more accurately capture and bill any computer usage of hotel phone lines. If that’s the case, the reason the customer should do business with you is because your product will generate $2 per room per night in incremental revenue.

如果产品带来的益处让顾客感觉良好，那么高效的暖气片或天然气销售员可能会回答“顾客会得到温暖舒适的房间”。（低效的暖气片销售员会认为顾客购买的是英热单位 (BTU)。）如果你的产品解决了某个问题，那么这个问题的答案应该用金钱来表达。例如，假设某个软件程序能让酒店更准确地记录和计费酒店电话线路的任何计算机使用情况。如果是这样，那么顾客应该与你做生意的理由是，你的产品将为每间客房每晚带来 2 美元的增量收入。

The Rainmaker answers the question “Why should the customer do business with us?” by calculating what economic benefits the product will give the customer and by calculating the consequences to the customer of not going with the recommended product. The Rainmaker determines how the customer is benefited directly and personally.

雨人决策者通过计算产品能给客户带来的经济效益，以及客户不选择推荐产品可能带来的后果，来回答“客户为什么要与我们做生意？”这个问题。雨人决策者确定客户如何获得直接且切身的利益。

The Rainmaker puts himself or herself in the customer’s shoes and answers the question “If I were the customer, how would this product benefit me?”

雨人会站在顾客的角度，回答“如果我是顾客，这个产品会给我带来什么好处？”这个问题。

• 3 •

• 3 •

Obey Marketing’s First Commandment

遵守营销的第一条戒律

T he first commandment of getting and keeping customers is to treat each customer as you would treat yourself. Do you like to be overcharged, underserved, put on endless hold, overbooked, told your room isn’t ready, falsely promised, shipped late, ignored, not thanked?

吸引并留住顾客的首要原则是善待每一位顾客，如同善待自己。您是否喜欢被多收费、服务不足、无休止地等待、超额预订、被告知房间未准备好、虚假承诺、延迟发货、被忽视、得不到感谢？

Always put yourself in the shoes of the good customer. Answer the question “What would I want if I were the customer?” The answer is what you should strive to provide.

永远站在优质顾客的角度。回答这个问题：“如果我是顾客，我想要什么？”答案就是你应该努力提供的。

This is important when dealing with the upset customer. When you are the upset customer, you want a full, uninterrupted hearing, you want to deal with someone with the authority to fix the problem, and you want a fair resolution. You don’t want to be sent a copy of the company’s warranty policy. You don’t want to be told to send another sample of your upholstery to the factory, get yet another professional couch cleaning, or be told the stains are of “indeterminate nature” and your claim is denied.

在处理不满的客户时，这一点至关重要。当您是不满的客户时，您希望得到全面、不间断的听证，您希望与有权解决问题的人交涉，并且您希望得到公平的解决方案。您肯定不希望收到公司保修政策的副本。您也不想被告知要将家具样品送回工厂，再进行一次专业的沙发清洁，或者被告知污渍“性质不明”，从而导致索赔被拒。

Remember, good customers are demanding. They may expect more from you than you believe is appropriate. What you want or how you want to be treated may not be good enough to satisfy your customers, but it’s a good starting place.

记住，好顾客要求很高。他们对你的期望可能超出你的预期。你的需求或你希望得到的待遇可能不足以让顾客满意，但这是一个很好的起点。

Deliver on your promise and you’ll bring rain.

兑现你的诺言，你就会带来雨水。

# ↩

• 4 •

• 4 •

Customers Don’t Care About You

顾客不在乎你

I n the selling arena, customers don’t care if you have a mortgage to pay. Customers don’t care if you need their business to win a contest. Customers don’t care why your shipments are late. Customers don’t care what you like, where you went to school, or what sports you play or played.

在销售领域，客户不在乎你是否有抵押贷款要偿还。客户不在乎你是否需要他们的生意来赢得比赛。客户不在乎你的发货为什么延迟。客户不在乎你喜欢什么，你在哪里上学，或者你从事或正在从事什么运动。

The only thing customers care about are themselves and their problem. You are in front of the customer only because the customer believes, if only a little bit, that you might be able to better his or her situation.

客户唯一关心的就是他们自己和他们的问题。你出现在客户面前，只是因为他们相信，哪怕只有一点点，你或许能够改善他们的处境。

You are there by invitation only. You must concentrate on the customer. You must be on high receive. You do not talk about yourself; rather, you ask probing, preplanned questions. You listen to what the customer says. Clarify. Summarize. Determine how you can help the customer and how your product solves the customer’s concern.

你只能受邀前往。你必须专注于客户。你必须保持高度的专注。你不要谈论自己，而是要提出一些预先计划好的、探究性的问题。你要倾听客户的诉求。澄清问题。总结问题。确定你如何帮助客户，以及你的产品如何解决客户的顾虑。

Rainmakers say “you”; they don’t say “I.”

祈雨者说的是“你”；他们不会说“我”。

# ↩

• 5 •

• 5 •

Always Precall Plan Every Sales Call

每次销售拜访前务必做好计划

A ppointments with decision makers are relatively rare events. Meetings with decision makers are crucial to getting the sale. Because of this, meetings with a decision maker must be carefully preplanned. Precall planning is particularly important when making the first call on a new customer and when making the last call—the one that concludes with an order.

与决策者的会面相对少见。与决策者的会面对于促成销售至关重要。因此，与决策者的会面必须经过精心的预先规划。在第一次拜访新客户以及最后一次拜访（最终促成订单的拜访）时，事先规划尤为重要。

Ninety percent of all sales calls are won or lost before the salesperson sees the customer. This is because so few salespeople actually plan the call. Too many salespeople believe experience is a substitute for precall planning; they think they don’t need to. Other salespeople do their precall planning on the way to a call. Others don’t even know how to precall plan. Some don’t know they should.

90% 的销售电话在销售人员见到客户之前就已经赢得或输掉了。这是因为很少有销售人员真正做好了电话计划。太多销售人员认为经验可以取代拜访前的计划；他们认为他们不需要这样做。有些销售人员在前往客户现场的途中做好了拜访前的计划。还有一些销售人员甚至不知道如何做好拜访前的计划。有些人甚至不知道自己应该这样做。

Rainmakers never waste a sales call: They always precall plan. It is typical for a Rainmaker to spend three hours planning for a fifteen-minute sales call. Planning and practicing for two days to two weeks for a single sales call is not uncommon.

雨人从不浪费任何一次销售电话：他们总是提前做好计划。雨人通常会花三个小时来准备一个十五分钟的销售电话。为了一次销售电话，他们甚至会花两天甚至两周来准备和练习，这种情况并不罕见。

One Rainmaker spent fifteen straight eight-hour days researching and planning a fifteen-minute sales call. The call was on the CEO of a leading company in a new industry. If this company adopted the Rainmaker’s product, almost certainly the other companies in the industry would follow. The Rainmaker made the sale and successfully used it as a case history to close other customers. This single sale saved the Rainmaker’s company and led to years of success.

一位Rainmaker连续15天，每天8小时，研究并策划一通15分钟的销售电话。这通电话的对象是一家新兴行业领先公司的首席执行官。如果这家公司采用了Rainmaker的产品，几乎可以肯定，行业内的其他公司也会纷纷效仿。这位Rainmaker成功完成了这笔交易，并成功地以此为案例，促成了其他客户的签约。这笔交易挽救了Rainmaker的公司，并为其带来了多年的成功。

A precall plan for a Rainmaker is like a preflight check for an airplane pilot. The great pilots never miss a single checkpoint before taking off or landing. If a pilot misses something, that pilot may be missing. If a salesperson misses something, the order may be missing.

Rainmaker 的预召计划就像飞机飞行员的飞行前检查一样。优秀的飞行员在起飞或降落前绝不会错过任何一个检查点。如果飞行员错过了什么，那他可能就错过了。如果销售人员错过了什么，那订单可能就没了。

A precall planning checklist should include:

呼叫前计划清单应包括：

  1. Written sales call objective.
    书面销售拜访目标。
  2. Needs-analysis questions to ask.
    需要询问的分析问题。
  3. Something to show.
    有东西可以展示。
  4. Anticipated customer concerns and objections.
    预见客户的顾虑和反对意见。
  5. Points of difference vis-à-vis competitors.
    与竞争对手的差异点。
  6. Meaningful benefits to customers.
    为客户带来切实的利益。
  7. Dollarization approach; investment return analysis.
    美元化方法；投资回报分析。
  8. Strategies to handle objections and eliminate customer concerns.
    处理异议和消除客户顾虑的策略。
  9. Closing strategies.
    结束策略。
  10. Expected surprises.
    预料之中的惊喜。

And plan to be flexible. If after sixty seconds into your two-hour painstakingly prepared presentation the customer says she will buy, stop talking, take the order, and gracefully leave. If the customer wants to do business with you, but in an entirely different manner than you expected, adjust to the change. Don’t be so intent on following your plan that you miss a customer’s cue. Be flexible.

并做好灵活的计划。如果在你精心准备的两小时演示进行到六十秒后，顾客表示要购买，请停止谈话，接受订单，然后优雅地离开。如果顾客想和你做生意，但方式与你预期的完全不同，请根据情况进行调整。不要过于专注于你的计划，而忽略了顾客的暗示。要灵活变通。

A Rainmaker never calls on a decision maker without a written precall plan.

如果没有书面的预先计划，雨人决不会拜访决策者。

• 6 •

• 6 •

Fish Where the Big Fish Are

大鱼出没的地方

W hen asked “What is the most important thing you need when you go fishing?” most people say “bait,” “pole,” “hooks,” and “beer.” Those are important, but the most important thing needed is fish! You can have the best boat on the prettiest lake with awesome tackle, but if there are no fish, you will go home empty-handed. If, however, you have only a raggedy old net but a little pond teeming with fish, your chances of a catch are much greater.

当被问到“钓鱼时最重要的东西是什么？”时，大多数人会说“鱼饵”、“鱼竿”、“鱼钩”和“啤酒”。这些固然重要，但最重要的是鱼！你可以在最美的湖面上驾着最好的船，配上一流的渔具，但如果没有鱼，你只能空手而归。然而，如果你只有一张破旧的渔网，却在一个鱼满为患的小池塘里，你捕到鱼的机会就大得多。

Where you cast your line is crucial to catching fish. This is also true for selling. Rainmakers fish where the big fish are. Rainmakers talk to customers who are familiar with their product, or who already use the product, or who have a high probability of using the product. Don’t waste your time trying to convince dairy farmers to buy horseshoes. And don’t waste your time selling hospital beds to hotels.

钓鱼的关键在于鱼竿的抛线位置。销售也是如此。“雨人”会去大鱼所在的地方钓鱼。“雨人”会与熟悉其产品、已经使用过该产品或很有可能使用该产品的客户沟通。不要浪费时间去说服奶农购买马蹄铁。也不要浪费时间去向酒店推销病床。

Big companies in an industry are generally better prospects than small companies in the same industry. Successful customers are generally better prospects than struggling customers. Customers who want your product are better targets than customers who need your product. (Customers who need your product may not know it. They must be educated, persuaded. This takes time and money. Customers who want your product are partially sold before they see you.)

同行业中的大公司通常比小公司拥有更好的前景。成功的客户通常比挣扎求存的客户拥有更好的前景。想要你的产品的客户比需要你的产品的客户更有吸引力。（需要你的产品的客户可能并不了解你的产品。你必须教育他们，说服他们。这需要时间和金钱。想要你的产品的客户在看到你之前就已经部分销售出去了。）

To a Rainmaker, the big sale is the trophy fish on the wall.

对于 Rainmaker 来说，最大的销售就是墙上的奖杯鱼。

• 7 •

• 7 •

Show Them the Money!

向他们展示金钱！

C ustomers buy for only two reasons: to feel good or to solve a problem. Going out to dinner, buying scuba equipment, or getting a new puppy fall into the “feel good” category. The prevailing purchase motivation for organizations is to solve a problem. The solution to the problem can always be expressed in financial terms—in dollars and cents. If a company invests $100,000 in advertising, they expect that advertising to generate $500,000 in sales. When a motor manufacturer replaces a cheap $.08 rubber o-ring with a $.10 viton o-ring, they expect to save $.30 per o-ring with reduced warranty claims. A tree surgeon uses a $900 saw because it cuts five times faster than a cheaper saw, saving him $50 a day in reduced labor costs.

顾客购买产品只有两个原因：感觉良好或解决问题。外出吃饭、购买潜水设备或养一只新小狗都属于“感觉良好”的类别。组织最主要的购买动机是解决问题。问题的解决方案总是可以用财务术语来表达——以美元和美分表示。如果一家公司在广告上投资 100,000 美元，他们预计这笔广告将带来 500,000 美元的销售额。当一家汽车制造商用 0.10 美元的氟橡胶 O 形圈替换廉价的 0.08 美元橡胶 O 形圈时，他们预计每个 O 形圈可节省 0.30 美元，同时减少保修索赔。一位树木外科医生使用 900 美元的锯子，因为它的切割速度是便宜锯子的五倍，通过减少人工成本，他每天可以节省 50 美元。

Rainmakers don’t sell fasteners or valves or washing machines or double-paned windows or tax audits or irrigation systems or training programs or golf clubs. Rainmakers sell money! They sell reduced downtime, fewer repairs, better gas mileage, higher deposit interest, increased output, decreased energy usage, more wheat per acre, more yardage per swing.

造雨人卖的不是紧固件、阀门、洗衣机、双层玻璃窗、税务审计、灌溉系统、培训项目或高尔夫球杆。造雨人卖的是钱！他们卖的是减少停机时间、减少维修、提高燃油效率、提高存款利息、增加产量、降低能源消耗、增加每英亩小麦产量、增加每次挥杆码数。

Rainmakers help the customer see the money. Rainmakers turn benefits into dollars. The plumber who generates the most revenue doesn’t charge $50 for a service call, he sells a clean, dry basement for $100, saving the customer’s thousand-dollar carpet.

造雨人帮助客户看到金钱。造雨人将收益转化为金钱。创造最高收入的水管工不会收取50美元的上门服务费，而是以100美元的价格出售一个干净干燥的地下室，从而为客户节省了价值数千美元的地毯。

The lock salesperson doesn’t sell locks, he sells security for valuables. The pool salesman doesn’t just sell recreation, he sells an increase in home value.

锁具销售员卖的不仅仅是锁，他卖的是贵重物品的安全保障。泳池销售员卖的不仅仅是娱乐，他卖的是房屋增值。

The number one salesperson for a company that made cough medicine never sold a single bottle of cough medicine. He was by far the leading salesperson, but he never sold a cough drop.

一家生产止咳药的公司的头号销售员，竟然连一瓶止咳药都没卖出去。他是销售业绩遥遥领先的销售员，却连一颗止咳糖都没卖出去。

The company made products for people with colds, sore throats, hay fever, and sinus conditions. The company made throat lozenges, cough drops, gargles, and sprays. The company trained its sales force on how the products worked, all about the product chemistry, and why their products were the best. The company’s success depended on how many cases of cough medicine and gargle it sold. That meant the company’s success depended on the demand for the product; the number of people with colds.

该公司生产针对感冒、咽喉痛、花粉症和鼻窦疾病等人群的产品。该公司生产润喉糖、止咳糖浆、漱口水和喷雾剂。该公司对销售人员进行了产品功效、化学成分以及其产品为何最佳的培训。公司的成功取决于止咳药和漱口水的销量。这意味着公司的成功取决于产品的需求量，即感冒患者的数量。

The company made its product available to the public by selling to pharmacies, to drugstore owners. In order to make its products more appealing to the drugstore owner than the competitors’ medicine, the salesperson’s company offered an incentive: For every five cases of products purchased the druggist could either get one case of product for free (to resell at retail prices) or a bank check for the equivalent purchase price of one case. (The free case or check were both worth $25.)

该公司通过向药店和药房老板销售产品，将产品推向公众。为了使其产品比竞争对手的药品更吸引药房老板，销售人员所在的公司提供了一项奖励：每购买五箱产品，药剂师可以免费获得一箱产品（以零售价转售），或者获得一张等值于一箱产品购买价的银行支票。（免费一箱或支票的价值均为25美元。）

The salesperson realized that his customers were not people with colds. His customers were the drugstore owners. (People with colds were the druggists’ customers.) So despite all the technical product training, unlike his colleagues, the number one salesperson never talked about the products’ formulas, strength, or soothing aspects.

这位销售员意识到，他的顾客并非感冒患者，而是药店老板。（感冒患者是药剂师的顾客。）因此，尽管接受了所有产品技术培训，这位一号销售员却从未像其他同事那样谈论过产品的配方、功效或舒缓功效。

The number one salesperson talked to the drugstore owners about money.

一号销售员和药店老板谈钱的事。

The salesperson would explain the five-case purchase incentive, then immediately ask, “What do you prefer, the cash or the free product?” Almost always, the drugstore owners would opt for the money.

销售人员会解释五种购买奖励，然后立即询问：“您想要什么，现金还是免费产品？”药店老板几乎总是会选择现金。

If the customer chose the money (in a bank check) the salesperson would then ask, “How much money do you want?”

如果顾客选择钱（银行支票），销售人员就会问：“您想要多少钱？”

The salesperson didn’t sell cures for coughs; he sold a rebate check of $25 for every five cases of product purchased. Getting more money meant buying more product, and that’s what many pharmacists did.

这位销售员卖的不是治咳嗽的药，而是每售出五箱产品，他就能获得一张25美元的返利支票。赚得越多，就意味着能买得更多产品，很多药剂师就是这么做的。

The number one salesperson sold money! All the other salespeople regaled druggists with facts on cough suppressant chemicals and breathe-free passages. They were far-distant followers in the contest.

排名第一的销售员卖出了不少钱！其他销售员则向药剂师们滔滔不绝地讲解着止咳药和通气方法。在这场竞争中，他们远远落后。

Always show the customer the money. Always dollarize (see “A Rainmaker Extra,” here ). Quantify the customer’s return on his investment in your product. Calculate the financial consequences to the customer—the cost of going without your solution.

务必向客户展示收益。务必将收益体现在金钱上（参见此处的“雨人额外福利”）。量化客户对你产品的投资回报。计算客户可能遭受的经济损失——放弃你的解决方案的成本。

Rainmakers don’t sell products; they sell the dollarized value the customer gets from the products.

Rainmakers 并不销售产品，他们销售的是客户从产品中获得的美元价值。

Rainmakers sell money.

祈雨者卖钱。

Earthquakes Don’t Count

地震不算数

Y ou either made the sale or you didn’t.

您要么完成销售，要么不完成销售。

No one wants to hear why you didn’t bring in the business. No one cares that “the peso was devalued,” or “the customer went bankrupt,” or “the economy is lousy,” or “a huge competitor opened next door.”

没人想听你为什么没能把生意做成。没人会在意“比索贬值了”、“客户破产了”、“经济不景气”或者“隔壁开了一家巨大的竞争对手”。

The hunter either comes home with the game or he doesn’t. His family eats or goes hungry. No one cares that “the rain washed away the deer tracks.”

猎人要么带着猎物回家，要么一无所获。他的家人要么吃饱，要么挨饿。没人在乎“雨水冲走了鹿的足迹”。

A young brand manager captured the attention of his company’s sales force by offering terrific prizes for hitting defined sales quotas. The contest rules were easy: reach your quota, you win; fall short, you lose. Three weeks before the contest deadline an earthquake hit Los Angeles. The California sales office was badly damaged and business was interrupted. The California sales team did not reach its quota.

一位年轻的品牌经理通过为达成既定销售配额的销售人员提供丰厚的奖励，吸引了公司销售团队的注意。比赛规则很简单：达到配额即获胜；未达标即失败。比赛截止日期前三周，洛杉矶发生了地震。加州销售办公室严重受损，业务中断。加州销售团队未能完成配额。

California was the largest market in the brand manager’s company. The California sales team had great influence in the company. The California sales team wanted the prizes, but the brand manager said no. The California sales team used all its muscle, and the powerful vice president of sales insisted the brand manager award California the prizes. The vice president argued that the California team missed its quota by “only a few percentage points” and “be reasonable… there was an earthquake.”

加州是这位品牌经理公司最大的市场。加州销售团队在公司中拥有巨大的影响力。他们想要这些奖项，但被品牌经理拒绝了。加州销售团队使出浑身解数，而这位掌权的销售副总裁坚持要求品牌经理将奖项授予加州团队。副总裁辩称，加州团队“只差几个百分点”就完成了目标，而且“理智点……当时地震了”。

The brand manager firmly stood his ground, and replied, “Earthquakes don’t count.”

品牌经理态度坚决地回答道：“地震不算。”

The next year there were record blizzards in Chicago, floods along the Mississippi, a brownout in New York City, a natural gas shortage, and political crises in Washington. The next year every region in the country hit its quota—California came in first—and everyone won a prize.

第二年，芝加哥遭遇了创纪录的暴风雪，密西西比河沿岸发生洪水，纽约市出现灯火管制，天然气短缺，华盛顿也爆发了政治危机。第二年，全国所有地区都完成了各自的配额——加州位居第一——每个人都获得了奖励。

Rainmakers don’t have excuses.

祈雨者没有借口。

Killer Sales Question #1

杀手级销售问题 #1

O ne of the four events that are inherent in every sale is scheduling an appointment with the decision maker. You can’t get the sale unless you talk to the decision maker. Getting appointments with busy decision makers is often difficult. Phone sellers often make preliminary calls to set up a phone conference, the appointment. Field salespeople know there is no substitute for the face-to-face meeting.

每笔销售中不可或缺的四件事之一就是与决策者预约会面。除非你与决策者沟通，否则你无法达成交易。与忙碌的决策者预约会面通常很困难。电话销售人员通常会先打电话预约电话会议。现场销售人员知道，没有什么可以取代面对面的会面。

Do the homework. Dollarize the reason why the customer should do business with you. Send a four- or five-sentence letter to the customer detailing the dollarized benefit of the product and promising a follow-up phone call. The objective of the letter is to get the customer to take the follow-up phone call. Good customers don’t ignore a compelling dollarization. They will take your call.

做好功课。用金钱来形容客户应该与你做生意的理由。给客户发一封四五句话的信，详细说明产品的金钱优势，并承诺会打电话跟进。这封信的目的是让客户接听后续电话。好的客户不会忽视令人信服的金钱优势。他们会接听你的电话。

When you have the customer on the phone, suggest a meeting, and then ask, “Do you have your appointment calendar handy?”

当您与客户通电话时，建议会面，然后询问：“您手边有预约日历吗？”

This is a killer sales question because it leads to that precious appointment over 90 percent of the time.

这是一个至关重要的销售问题，因为 90% 以上的时间它都能促成宝贵的预约。

Then ask, “Is Tuesday at three OK?” “No.” “How about Thursday at eight-thirty A.M. ?” “No.” “How about next Friday at three?” “Fine.” “OK, great, the meeting will take about twenty minutes. See you at three. Thanks.”

然后问：“星期二三点可以吗？”“不行。”“星期四早上八点半怎么样？”“不行。”“下周五三点怎么样？”“可以。”“好的，太好了，会议大约需要二十分钟。三点见。谢谢。”

Rainmakers make appointments to make rain.

祈雨者会预约降雨。

• 10 •

Stand Out! Send a Letter!

脱颖而出！发送信件！

F irst -class-stamp-bearing letters are vanishing. First-class mail is down more than 30 percent since the rise of e-mail and other electronic communications. The trend is decidedly downward.

贴有一级邮票的信件正在消失。自从电子邮件和其他电子通讯方式兴起以来，一级邮件的数量下降了30%以上。这种趋势明显下降。

Most first-class mail consists of impersonal bills, checks, and legal notices. The volume of business letters has fallen below 1970 levels.

大多数一等邮件都包含非个人性质的账单、支票和法律通知。商业信函的数量已降至1970年的水平以下。

Business letters are so rare, they stand out. Business letters are a point of difference. One business letter has more impact than one thousand e-mails. A well-written business letter opens doors, gets appointments, and cracks new accounts.

商务信函非常罕见，因此格外引人注目。商务信函本身就与众不同。一封商务信函比一千封电子邮件更有影响力。一封写得好的商务信函能打开商机，促成预约，并赢得新客户。

Here is an example of a business-getting business letter:

以下是一封商业信函的示例：

Dear Prospect:

亲爱的潜在客户：

John Smith of ABC Company suggested we meet. He believes you could reap enormous benefits, as did he, from our new but proven sealing technology.

ABC公司的约翰·史密斯建议我们见面。他相信，我们全新且成熟的密封技术能为您带来巨大的益处，他也是这么认为的。

Based on experience and research, we have a high degree of confidence you can save more than $100,000 per month in reduced downtime.

根据经验和研究，我们高度相信，通过减少停机时间，您每月可以节省 100,000 美元以上。

It will take ten minutes to show you how this is possible.

我们需要花十分钟来向您展示这是如何实现的。

If I don’t hear from you in a few days, please expect a polite follow-up.

如果几天后我还没有收到您的回复，请期待礼貌的跟进。

Sealingly yours,

谨致问候，

Rainmaker

雨人

Always Take the Best Seat in a Restaurant

总是在餐厅里占据最好的座位

I f you take a customer or prospective customer to breakfast, lunch, or dinner, always take the best seat. You take the seat with your back to the wall. You take the seat that looks out onto the golf course or marina or street. You don’t want your customer’s attention to wander. You don’t want your customer to check out who is coming and going.

如果你带顾客或潜在客户去吃早餐、午餐或晚餐，一定要选最好的座位。背靠墙的座位，面朝高尔夫球场、码头或街道的座位。你肯定不希望顾客的注意力分散，也不想让顾客留意来来往往的人。

You want your customer to focus on you. You want your customer as involved as possible in answering your questions and evaluating your recommendations. You do not want his concentration or his considerations interrupted by someone or something more interesting than your software package or office machine or mutual fund or design proposal or refrigeration equipment.

您希望客户专注于您。您希望客户尽可能地参与回答您的问题并评估您的建议。您不希望他的注意力或思考被比您的软件包、办公设备、共同基金、设计方案或制冷设备更有趣的人或事打断。

Your customer has invested some of his precious time to meet with you. It is only polite for you to optimize his time investment, and not let it be squandered by distractions.

您的客户投入了宝贵的时间与您会面。出于礼貌，您应该优化他的时间投入，避免让其被其他干扰所浪费。

If the customer takes you to breakfast, lunch, or dinner, you still take the best seat.

如果顾客带你去吃早餐、午餐或晚餐，你仍然会占据最好的座位。

Don’t Drink Coffee on a Sales Call

不要在销售电话中喝咖啡

A sales call is a sales call. It’s not teatime at the Rainbow Room. You are not there to “wake up and smell the coffee.” You are there to do business.

销售拜访就是销售拜访。这不是彩虹屋里的下午茶时间。你来这里不是为了“醒来闻闻咖啡的香味”。你来这里是为了做生意。

The duration of the average sales call is eighteen to twenty minutes. You do not have time to go get the coffee, pour the coffee, stir in the cream, or drink the coffee. You have to maximize time and concentrate on your objective. Drinking coffee wastes time and interferes with your presentation. You can’t take notes with a coffee cup in your hand.

平均一次销售电话的时长为18到20分钟。你没有时间去冲咖啡、倒咖啡、搅拌奶油或喝咖啡。你必须最大限度地利用时间，专注于你的目标。喝咖啡浪费时间，还会干扰你的演讲。你不可能一边拿着咖啡杯一边做笔记。

A sales call was scheduled three months in advance. It was difficult to get an appointment with the harried decision maker who was responsible for buying high-ticket (over $300,000 a copy) computer peripheral packages. The salesperson and a consultant to his company met for breakfast to preplan the sales call. When offered, the salesperson said he did not drink coffee.

一次销售拜访提前三个月安排好了。要约见一位负责采购高价（每台超过30万美元）电脑外设套件的决策者可不容易。这位销售人员和公司一位顾问一起吃了早餐，商量好了这次拜访。当这位销售人员主动提出要约时，他却说自己不喝咖啡。

The duo arrived promptly and was met by the prospective customer, the Computer Center Manager. The customer was friendly and graciously asked if his guests would like some coffee. “That would be great,” said the salesperson who did not drink coffee. So off they trudged to the coffee room, and began the ritual. They returned to the customer’s office. The salesperson put his coffee on the worktable, but accidentally set the cup on a heavy-duty marking pen. The coffee spilled over the worktable. The customer scrambled to save the blueprints. Paper towels were needed.

两人准时到达，迎接他们的是潜在客户——计算机中心经理。这位客户态度友好，彬彬有礼地询问客人是否想喝咖啡。“太好了，”不喝咖啡的销售员说道。于是，他们拖着沉重的步子走到咖啡室，开始了例行公事。他们回到客户的办公室。销售员把咖啡放在工作台上，却不小心把杯子压在了一支厚重的记号笔上。咖啡洒了一地。客户慌忙去抢蓝图。需要用纸巾。

The sales call ultimately restarted. Ten minutes into the call everything looked promising: The customer was in agreement, he had a need for the package, and he had the budget. There was a knock on the door and someone from the Computer Center anxiously told the manager that “one of the main servers is in a degraded mode!” The prospective customer jumped to his feet and, while politely excusing himself, invited the salesperson to phone in a few weeks to see if they could reschedule. And out the door vanished the customer… and the sale.

销售电话终于重新开始了。通话进行了十分钟，一切看起来都很有希望：客户同意了，他确实需要这个套餐，而且预算也足够。这时，门响了，计算机中心的人焦急地告诉经理：“其中一个主服务器处于降级模式！”潜在客户一下子跳了起来，一边礼貌地告辞，一边邀请销售人员几周后再打电话过来，看看能否重新安排时间。然后，客户就消失了……销售也随之消失了。

Coffee killed that sale.

咖啡扼杀了这笔销售。

If the customer asks if you want coffee, say “No, thank you” and get to work.

如果顾客问您是否需要咖啡，请说“不，谢谢”然后开始工作。

And don’t drink coffee on the plane, or in the car, on the way to a sales call. A spill can kill.

还有，不要在飞机上、车里或去销售拜访的路上喝咖啡。洒出来会致命。

You’re Not at Lunch to Eat Lunch

你不是来吃午饭的

I f you are at a cocktail party with customers, you are not there to party. If you are playing golf with a client, you are not there to play golf.

如果你和客户一起参加鸡尾酒会，你来这里不是为了参加派对。如果你和客户一起打高尔夫球，你来这里不是为了打高尔夫球。

These are business meetings or sales calls or both. You do business at business meetings. Some salespeople forget the priority. They actually care what golf score they shoot. And at the nineteenth hole, instead of closing the deal, they are still talking about the thirty-five-foot putt they made on the front nine.

这些是商务会议或销售电话，或者两者兼而有之。你在商务会议上谈生意。有些销售人员忘记了重点。他们实际上在乎自己打出的高尔夫球成绩。到了第十九洞，他们不是在谈成交易，而是还在谈论前九洞那个35英尺的推杆。

A luncheon meeting with a client or prospective customer is a sales call with tableware. You are there to ask questions, to listen, and to get a commitment. You are not there to sample the bronzed shrimp Creole or do research for a restaurant review. Don’t waste time perusing the intricacies of the menu. Don’t ask the waiter how anything is prepared. Don’t ask the waitress if a rasher of bacon is three strips or four. Food is not your focus—the customer is!

与客户或潜在客户的午餐会就像是拿着餐具的推销。你在那里是为了提问、倾听并获得承诺。你不是来品尝克里奥尔烤虾或为餐厅点评做研究的。不要浪费时间仔细研究菜单的复杂细节。不要问服务员任何菜品是如何制作的。不要问服务员一片培根是三条还是四条。食物不是你的重点——顾客才是！

Order something easy to eat. Order only one course. Order something inexpensive.

点一些容易吃的。只点一道菜。点一些便宜的。

It is OK if you don’t eat anything. It is rude to talk with food in your mouth. It is impolite to survey your dish when your customer is talking. And it is hard to take notes with a fork in your hand.

如果你什么都不吃也没关系。嘴里含着食物说话很不礼貌。顾客说话时，你盯着盘子看也很不礼貌。而且，手里拿着叉子记笔记也很困难。

It’s not about lunch. It’s about getting the customer’s commitment, getting the bill, and getting on to the next appointment.

重要的不是午餐，而是获得顾客的承诺、结账，然后去赴下一个预约。

Never Wear a Pen in Your Shirt Pocket

切勿将笔放在衬衫口袋里

I t’s your first meeting with a prospective client. You prepared carefully. You dressed with care. You are ready to persuade the customer to do business with you because of your meticulous attention to detail.

这是你与潜在客户的第一次会面。你精心准备，精心打扮。你准备好凭借对细节的细致关注，说服客户与你做生意。

Your designer pen, in your left breast pocket, has bled. A startling blue stain has become a focal point for your customer. She can’t take her eyes off your ruined shirt. She can’t get completely involved in your presentation. She feels trapped. She is embarrassed for you. She is too polite to tell you, and is nervous about what to do when you discover the leak. She is hoping the meeting will end quickly. She is hoping to avoid witnessing your inevitable discomfort.

你左胸口袋里的名牌笔漏水了。一处令人震惊的蓝色污渍成了顾客的眼中钉。她目不转睛地盯着你那件被毁的衬衫。她无法全身心地投入到你的演示中。她感到无助，为你感到尴尬。她太客气了，没告诉你，而且很紧张，不知道你发现漏水后该怎么办。她希望会议快点结束，不想目睹你那不可避免的尴尬。

Your leaky pen killed the sale.

你的漏水笔毁了这次销售。

And you don’t want ballpoint streaks on your shirt, either. Buy shirts without pockets, and keep your pens in your briefcase.

你肯定也不想衬衫上沾满圆珠笔的痕迹。买没有口袋的衬衫，把笔放在公文包里。

Rainmakers do nothing that might decrease the odds of making the sale.

催雨者不会采取任何可能降低销售成功率的行动。

Killer Sales Question #2

杀手销售问题 #2

A fter exhaustive homework and a careful needs analysis, the Rainmaker knows if he has a solution to the customer’s problem. The Rainmaker has dollarized the solution and knows how much money the customer will get from the solution, and how much it will cost the customer to go without the solution.

经过详尽的准备和仔细的需求分析，雨人知道自己是否有解决客户问题的解决方案。雨人已经将解决方案转化为金钱，并且知道客户能从中获得多少钱，以及如果没有这个解决方案，客户将付出多少代价。

The Rainmaker understands that sometimes a customer will ignore the facts, or will stay disengaged from the decision-making process, resulting in a “no sale.” The customer must be engaged, and must be in agreement.

Rainmaker 深知，有时顾客会忽略事实，或不参与决策过程，最终导致“销售失败”。因此，必须让顾客参与进来，并达成一致。

To get the customer involved, and to begin the necessary chain of positive agreements and commitments, the Rainmaker asks a powerful question that taps into the sense of free will and independence that is part of human nature.

为了让顾客参与进来，并开始必要的一系列积极协议和承诺，雨人提出了一个强有力的问题，这个问题触及了人性的自由意志和独立意识。

The Rainmaker asks the customer, “Based on analysis, it looks like you can save $180,000 per year with the solution. Can I assume there are probably a number of things that have to be done before you are completely comfortable with this approach? OK, so before we get into this in any depth, can I get your agreement on the analysis? Will you look at the facts and decide for yourself if they make sense?”

雨人问客户：“根据分析，该解决方案似乎每年可以为您节省 18 万美元。请问，在您完全接受这个方案之前，可能还需要做很多事情吗？好的，在我们深入讨论之前，能否请您同意我的分析？您能否先看看这些事实，自己判断一下这些分析是否合理？”

This is a killer sales question.

这是一个关键的销售问题。

To say to the customer “Will you decide for yourself?” is almost rhetorical because the answer is so seemingly obvious. The customer is certainly going to decide for herself. So she will answer yes, and will silently think, perhaps say aloud, “Of course I will decide for myself.”

问顾客“您自己决定吗？”几乎是反问，因为答案显而易见。顾客肯定会自己决定。所以她会回答“是”，然后默默思考，或许还会大声说出来：“我当然会自己决定。”

If the facts bear out the salesperson’s claim of saving $180,000, then for the customer to reject the solution, she must contradict her answer and admit she can’t decide for herself. This is an admission most customers won’t make.

如果事实证明销售人员确实节省了18万美元，那么顾客要想拒绝这个解决方案，就必须反驳销售人员的说法，承认自己无法决定。大多数顾客都不会承认这一点。

By agreeing to decide for herself, the customer eliminates the option of not deciding. The customer is now engaged and can’t ignore the facts. One way or another, the customer will make a decision. If the solution benefits her—as it must—she will buy.

通过同意自己做决定，顾客就排除了不做决定的可能性。顾客现在参与其中，无法忽视事实。无论如何，顾客都会做出决定。如果解决方案对她有利——而且必然如此——她就会购买。

Rainmakers Turn Customer Objections into Customer Objectives

雨人将客户反对意见转化为客户目标

C ustomers always have concerns or issues that must be satisfied before they will buy. Customers are concerned about price, affordability, delivery, reliability, size, color, warranty, availability, and myriad other issues. These concerns are sometimes spoken and sometimes not. These concerns vary by customer and vary in importance. A concern that is a deal breaker to one customer is a detail to another. These concerns are prepurchase objections to the salesperson’s proposal, whatever it may be. When the customer says, “The motor is too loud,” he is objecting to the noise of the product. When the customer says, “I don’t like forest green,” she is objecting to the color.

顾客在购买之前总会有一些需要解决的顾虑或问题。顾客关心价格、可负担性、配送、可靠性、尺寸、颜色、保修、供货情况以及无数其他问题。这些顾虑有时会说出来，有时则不会。这些顾虑因顾客而异，重要性也各不相同。对一个顾客来说可能成为交易障碍的顾虑，对另一个顾客来说可能只是一个细节问题。这些顾虑是顾客在购买前对销售人员的提议提出的异议，无论提议是什么。当顾客说“发动机声音太大”时，他反对的是产品的噪音。当顾客说“我不喜欢森林绿”时，她反对的是颜色。

Rainmakers welcome customer objections because they know objections are simply the way customers express their desires. The Rainmaker knows that when the customer says, “Your price is too high,” the customer’s goal is to get the proper value for the money invested. The objection tells the Rainmaker that the customer does not yet have enough information to make a positive buying decision.

雨人欢迎顾客提出异议，因为他们知道异议只是顾客表达愿望的方式。雨人深知，当顾客说“你的价格太高”时，顾客的目标是获得与其投入的金钱相符的合理价值。异议表明，顾客尚未掌握足够的信息来做出积极的购买决定。

The Rainmaker always turns a customer objection into a mutual—customer/Rainmaker—objective. The Rainmaker, in question form, restates the customer’s objection as an objective. To illustrate: The customer says, “Your delivery time is too long.” The Rainmaker responds, “So our objective is to get you the product when you want it, correct?”

雨人总是能将客户的反对意见转化为双方共同的目标——客户/雨人。雨人会以提问的形式，将客户的反对意见重新表述为目标。举例来说：客户说：“你们的送货时间太长了。” 雨人会回答：“所以我们的目标是在您需要的时候把产品送到您手中，对吗？”

Only Rainmakers understand the brilliant subtlety of turning objections into objectives. First, this technique changes the tone of the language from adversarial to positive. Second, the customer’s yes response is an agreement—an invitation to continue the discussion. Third, the Rainmaker can now ask more questions to perfectly understand the customer’s concern and to move to a mutually acceptable solution. For example, the Rainmaker might ask, “When exactly do you need the product?” Then say, “If you will commit today to a six-month purchase agreement, we can forecast monthly shipments, thereby ensuring that you will get the product on the first of the month, every month. Why don’t we give this a try for six months?”

只有“雨人”懂得将反对意见转化为目标的精妙之处。首先，这种技巧将语言的语气从对抗性转变为积极性。其次，客户的“是”回应本身就是一种同意——一种继续讨论的邀请。第三，雨人现在可以提出更多问题，以便更好地理解客户的顾虑，并最终找到双方都能接受的解决方案。例如，雨人可能会问：“您具体什么时候需要这款产品？”然后说：“如果您今天同意签订一份为期六个月的购买协议，我们可以预测每月的发货量，从而确保您每个月都能在每月的第一天收到产品。不如我们试试六个月？”

Rainmakers believe that objections are the way customers mask pleas for help and information. Rainmakers encourage objections, especially the hidden or unspoken ones. Rainmakers know that the sale cannot be made until every customer concern, no matter how trivial it seems, is satisfactorily handled. Consequently, if the sale is not made, Rainmakers always ask, “Is there anything else that concerns you?” Or, “What else may be prohibiting us from moving ahead?”

Rainmakers 认为，客户提出的异议是掩盖其寻求帮助和信息请求的方式。Rainmakers 鼓励提出异议，尤其是那些隐晦或未明说的异议。Rainmakers 深知，只有客户的每个顾虑，无论多么微不足道，都得到令人满意的解决，销售才能达成。因此，如果销售未能达成，Rainmakers 总会询问：“您还有什么其他顾虑吗？”或者，“还有什么阻碍我们继续前进？”

Rainmakers always probe for objections. Rainmakers love objections.

求雨者总是会探寻反对意见。求雨者喜欢反对意见。

Always Make a “Mid-Job, Next-Job” Recommendation

始终提出“工作中期、下一份工作”建议

T he Rainmaker is always thinking about how his company can help the customer, how the customer’s sales, profits, or well-being can be bettered. The Rainmaker knows that the customer’s continuing success is the only basis for the Rainmaker’s success.

雨人始终思考着自己的公司如何帮助客户，如何提升客户的销售额、利润或福祉。雨人深知，客户的持续成功是雨人成功的唯一基石。

The Rainmaker is always alert for the next job, the next assignment, the next sale. The Rainmaker knows that the easiest next sale is to a current customer. Current customers know the seller; they have an emotional investment in him and in his company. After all, the customer took a risk and hired or bought product from the Rainmaker’s company. The customer knows if the Rainmaker and his firm delivered on their promise. If the Rainmaker’s company successfully delivered the solution, the customer is grateful. Grateful customers are loyal customers.

雨人总是时刻关注着下一项工作、下一个任务、下一笔销售。雨人深知，最容易的下一笔销售就是面向现有客户。现有客户了解销售人员；他们对销售人员及其公司有着情感上的投入。毕竟，客户承担了风险，从雨人公司租用或购买了产品。客户知道雨人及其公司是否兑现了承诺。如果雨人公司成功交付了解决方案，客户就会心怀感激。心怀感激的客户才是忠诚的客户。

Midway through one project with a customer, the Rainmaker proposes another way in which the Rainmaker’s company can help the customer. This is the “mid-job, next-job” memo or recommendation letter. Presenting a “mid-job, next-job” e-mail is a Rainmaker rule.

在与客户合作的一个项目进行到一半时，Rainmaker 会提出公司可以为客户提供的另一种帮助方式。这就是“工作中期，下一份工作”的备忘录或推荐信。发送“工作中期，下一份工作”的电子邮件是 Rainmaker 的一项规则。

The landscaper, in the midst of sodding the yard, suggests a rock wall to reduce runoff and to enhance the property. The caterer, overwhelmingly busy serving a summer party, reminds her host that Christmas is only five months away. The lawyer, submerged in the details of a complicated estate plan, asks her client if her firm can do the client’s upcoming house purchase closing.

园艺师正在院子里铺草皮，建议建一堵石墙，以减少径流并提升房屋美感。宴会承办人正忙于准备一场夏日派对，提醒主人离圣诞节只有五个月了。律师正忙于复杂的遗产规划细节，询问客户她的律所能否承办即将到来的购房手续。

Your customer doesn’t know all you can do for her. Only you know. By the time you are halfway through your current job you should know how else you can help your customer. When you are in the middle of a job, begin selling the next one.

你的客户并不知道你能为她做多少。只有你自己知道。当你完成当前工作一半时，你应该知道还能如何帮助你的客户。当你正在做一项工作时，就开始推销下一项工作。

Rainmakers always have a mid-job, next-job action plan.

造雨者总是有一个中期工作和下一项工作的行动计划。

Treat Everybody You Meet as a Potential Client

把你遇到的每个人都视为潜在客户

R ainmakers see the world, and everyone in it, as their market. Rainmakers know the world is small. They know that everyone knows someone. They know that anyone can become a client, or refer a client, or recommend a client, or scuttle a promising relationship.

造雨人将世界及其中的每一个人视为他们的市场。造雨人深知世界很小。他们知道每个人都认识彼此。他们知道任何人都可能成为客户，或者推荐客户，或者推荐客户，或者破坏一段有希望的合作关系。

Rainmakers treat nonclients as they do existing customers. They are polite to everyone. Rainmakers view everyone as influential. They know that business can come from unexpected places. They know that something they did ten years ago might result in business today.

造雨人对待非客户如同对待现有客户一样。他们对每个人都彬彬有礼。造雨人视每个人都有影响力。他们知道生意可能来自意想不到的地方。他们知道十年前做的事情，今天可能会带来生意。

There are no “little people” to the Rainmaker. They do not berate the waiter because the kitchen is slow. They do not get angry with the person at the ticket counter because the airline delays or cancels a flight. Everyone is treated with courtesy. The Rainmaker is as respectful and polite to the guy who mows his lawn as he is to the president of the company that makes the lawn mowers.

在“雨人”眼中，没有“小人物”。他们不会因为厨房工作慢而责骂服务员。他们也不会因为航班延误或取消而对售票处的人发火。每个人都受到礼貌对待。“雨人”对待修剪草坪的工人，就像对待生产割草机的公司总裁一样，都同样尊重和礼貌。

A wire and cable salesman had a good relationship with the top management of a client company in Florida. The first person he met on every sales call at this customer was the company’s receptionist, an efficient, organized young woman. Part of her job was keeping the sales appointment schedule. Although she was not the person who bought wire and cable, and was never involved in the decision making, the salesman always treated her courteously. The salesman always waited patiently if there were delays, never making insistent demands—as did other salespeople. The salesman never implied his importance by dropping the name of the executive vice president, the person he was there to see, as did others. The salesman always thanked the receptionist for her help, and always made sure to say good-bye to her.

一位电线电缆销售员与佛罗里达州一家客户公司的高层管理人员关系良好。每次拜访这位客户，他见到的第一个人就是公司的接待员，一位高效、做事有条理的年轻女士。她的工作职责之一是安排销售预约。虽然她并非电线电缆的采购员，也从未参与决策，但这位销售员对她总是彬彬有礼。即使出现延误，这位销售员也总是耐心等待，从不像其他销售员那样提出过分的要求。这位销售员也从不像其他人那样，通过提及他此次拜访的执行副总裁的名字来暗示自己的重要性。这位销售员总是感谢接待员的帮助，并且总是确保与她道别。

Eighteen years later, the receptionist is now the executive vice president of the company. With her influence, her company became the wire and cable salesman’s biggest account.

十八年后，这位接待员如今已成为公司的执行副总裁。凭借她的影响力，她的公司成为了电线电缆销售员最大的客户。

Don’t make unnecessary enemies. Why be unlikable? Who is ever helped by unpleasant behavior? Pleasant people often appear self-controlled and confident. Customers like that.

不要树敌。何必招人讨厌？令人不快的行为对谁有帮助呢？友善的人通常表现得自律且自信。顾客喜欢这样的人。

The Rainmaker knows that anybody can help or hurt.

雨人知道任何人都可以提供帮助或造成伤害。

• 19 •

• 19 •

Heed the Biggest Buy Signal

留意最大的买入信号

A “buy signal” is something a customer does that indicates his or her willingness to purchase. When you ask a group of salespeople to state the biggest (most important) buy signals, they will usually list “the customer smiles,” “the customer asks about terms,” “the customer asks technical questions,” “the customer says yes,” and so on. These are all important buy signals. But the biggest buy signal is when the customer agrees to see you. The biggest buy signal is the sales call appointment.

“购买信号”是指客户做出的表明其购买意愿的行为。当你让一组销售人员说出最重要的购买信号时，他们通常会列出“客户微笑”、“客户询问条款”、“客户提出技术问题”、“客户同意”等等。这些都是重要的购买信号。但最大的购买信号是客户同意与你见面。最大的购买信号是销售拜访预约。

Today’s decision makers are usually too busy to see a salesperson unless the customer has a problem. Busy customers will not see a salesperson to chat, or talk about baseball. Busy customers are not doing a survey on the latest fashions salespeople are wearing. If the customer agrees to see you, it is because the customer wants something, needs something, has a problem. It is your job—the Rainmaker’s job—to find out what that is.

如今的决策者通常太忙了，除非客户有问题，否则没时间见销售人员。忙碌的客户不会找销售人员闲聊，或者聊棒球。忙碌的客户不会调查销售人员的最新时尚穿搭。如果客户同意见你，那是因为他们想要什么、需要什么，或者遇到了问题。你的工作——“雨人”的工作——就是找出他们想要什么、需要什么。

You find out what the customer wants on a sales call. When the customer agrees to see you, he or she knows it is a sales call, knows that you are a salesperson. The customer knows something about your product. The customer knows something about your competition. Consequently, the agreement to see you is a setting of the table to do business.

你在销售拜访中了解客户的需求。当客户同意与你见面时，他或她知道这是一次销售拜访，知道你是一名销售人员。客户对你的产品有所了解，也对你的竞争对手有所了解。因此，与你见面的协议是为开展业务奠定基础。

Rainmakers understand this reality, and it gives them bedrock confidence to make the sale.

Rainmakers 了解这一现实，这为他们完成销售提供了坚实的信心。

And always show up. Never blow off a sales call. Never be late.

一定要准时到达。千万不要错过销售拜访。千万不要迟到。

Killer Sales Question #3

杀手级销售问题 #3

T he customer says to you, “We are also interviewing [or “working with,” or “buying from”] ABC company. They are a good company, and their prices are better than yours.”

客户对你说：“我们也在面试（或“与……合作”或“从……购买”）ABC公司。他们是一家好公司，而且价格比你们的更优惠。”

The customer is actually saying, “Tell me why I should buy from you.” The customer already knows ABC is a good company. The customer already knows ABC’s prices are better than yours. The customer knew this before he agreed to see you! So, why did the customer agree to see you? The customer agreed to see you because there is something about ABC that makes the customer uneasy. You must underscore that unease.

客户实际上是在问：“告诉我为什么我应该从你这里买。” 客户已经知道ABC是一家好公司。客户已经知道ABC的价格比你的更优惠。客户在同意与你见面之前就知道了这一点！那么，客户为什么同意与你见面呢？客户同意与你见面是因为ABC的某些方面让他感到不安。你必须强调这种不安。

Because you have preplanned the call, you are forearmed with how you and your company differ from ABC.

因为您已经预先计划好了通话，所以您已经了解您和您的公司与 ABC 的不同之处。

You answer exactly as follows: “Yes, that is a good company. Would you like to know our points of difference?”

您的回答如下：“是的，那是一家好公司。您想知道我们的不同之处吗？”

This is a killer sales question.

这是一个关键的销售问题。

Your response does not knock the competitor. To do so would be to impugn the intelligence of the customer. In fact, you do not even repeat the competitor’s name.

你的回复并没有打击竞争对手。这样做会损害客户的智商。事实上，你甚至没有重复竞争对手的名字。

The customer will answer yes because this is precisely the question he wants answered. He wants to know the difference between you and ABC so he can decide to go with you.

客户会回答“是”，因为这正是他想要的答案。他想知道你和ABC的区别，这样才能决定是否选择你。

Your answer, your point of difference, will be forever what the customer thinks about you vis-à-vis the competitor. You will own that position.

你的答案，你的差异点，将永远决定客户对你与竞争对手的看法。你将占据这个位置。

Your point of difference (P.O.D.) should be an offset to the competitor. It need not be better or worse than what the competitor does—just different. Your P.O.D. should be information—or a new slant that the customer doesn’t know. With new and different information, the customer can change his mind without loss of face or criticism.

你的差异点（P.O.D.）应该能够抵消竞争对手的不足。它不必比竞争对手做得更好或更差——只要与众不同就行。你的差异点应该是信息，或者是一种客户不知道的新视角。有了新的、不同的信息，客户就可以改变主意，而不会丢脸或受到批评。

The headmaster of an all-boys private prep school in Connecticut knew he competed with co-ed prep schools and high schools for good students. In meetings with prospective students and their parents, the headmaster would ask, “Where else are you looking?” Predictably, the name of an excellent co-ed school would be mentioned. The headmaster would look thoughtful (but would not nod his head, which would suggest approval) and then ask, “Yes, I know that school. Would you be interested in our points of difference?”

康涅狄格州一所私立男校的校长知道，他要与男女混合的预科学校和高中竞争优秀学生。在与潜在学生及其家长见面时，校长会问：“你们还在寻找什么学校？”不出所料，一所优秀的男女混合学校的名字就会被提及。校长会若有所思（但不会点头，表示赞同），然后问道：“是的，我知道那所学校。你有兴趣了解一下我们的不同之处吗？”

The headmaster would then say, “As you know, this school is boys only. Our point of difference is that our boys are not distracted from their studies, because there are no girls in the classrooms or locker rooms. Wouldn’t you agree that more concentration on studies will make it easier to get into, and to succeed at, a good college?”

校长会说：“你知道，这所学校只招收男生。我们学校的不同之处在于，我们的男生不会因为教室和更衣室里没有女生而分心。你不觉得，更专注于学习更容易考上一所好大学，并在那里取得成功吗？”

In an age when single-sex schools are more and more a rarity, this all-boys prep school not only survives, it flourishes. (Incidentally, if the “all-boys, no-girls” point of difference weren’t meaningful to the customer, the headmaster had several more.)

在单性别学校越来越少见的时代，这所全男校不仅生存了下来，而且发展得相当繁荣。（顺便说一句，如果“全男无女”的差异对顾客来说不重要，校长还有更多其他的差异。）

“Me too” marketers are lazy, or noncreative, or have an inferiority complex. Rainmakers always find a difference. Rainmakers always invite customers to evaluate a point of difference. And the point of difference is just that—a difference. It need not be “better.” The customer needs to see a difference, new information, so he can change his mind or change the minds of his colleagues. Some people like blueberry pie and some like rhubarb. Each is different from the other, not necessarily better. So when the pie customer says to the blueberry pie salesperson, “I like rhubarb pie,” the salesperson responds, “Fine, would you like to know our point of difference? Unlike any other kind of pie, this pie is made with fresh, wild blueberries. Would you like to try a piece?”

“跟风”营销者要么懒惰，要么缺乏创造力，要么有自卑感。造雨人总能找到不同之处。造雨人总是邀请顾客评估不同之处。而不同之处仅仅是不同而已。它不必“更好”。顾客需要看到不同之处，看到新信息，这样他才能改变主意，或者改变同事的想法。有些人喜欢蓝莓派，有些人喜欢大黄派。两者各有不同，并不一定更好。所以当顾客对蓝莓派销售员说“我喜欢大黄派”时，销售员会回答说“好的，您想知道我们的不同之处吗？与其他派不同，这种派是用新鲜的野生蓝莓做的。您想尝一块吗？”

Rainmakers sell that which is different.

Rainmakers 销售的产品与众不同。

• 21 •

• 21 •

Always Return Every Call Every Day

每天回复每个电话

R eturning phone calls is a basic courtesy. But not many people do it. Rainmakers return all calls every day. They return everyone’s calls—customers, prospects, suppliers, job-seekers, parents. Rainmakers are not too big, too important, too busy for anyone.

回电话是基本的礼貌，但很少有人会这么做。“雨人”每天都会回所有电话。他们会回复所有人的电话——客户、潜在客户、供应商、求职者、家长。“雨人”不会因为规模太大、重要或繁忙而对任何人不敬。

Fast return of phone calls is a point of difference.

快速回复电话是其不同之处。

When you return a person’s phone call, that person feels respected, important, listened to. When you don’t return a call, the caller feels you don’t care, gets agitated, is less positive toward you.

当你回电话时，对方会感到被尊重、被重视、被倾听。当你不回电话时，对方会觉得你不在乎，变得焦躁不安，对你的态度也会不那么积极。

There is no excuse for not returning phone calls. It is nearly always acceptable to leave a voice-mail message if the person whose call you are returning is unavailable.

没有任何理由不回电话。如果对方无法接听，留下语音留言几乎总是可以接受的。

Rainmakers love leaving voice-mail messages on weekends and before and after business hours. This shows that the Rainmaker is thinking about the customer and working for him or her all the time. It also allows the Rainmaker extra time to better prepare for the upcoming two-way conversation.

Rainmaker 们喜欢在周末以及工作时间前后留下语音留言。这表明 Rainmaker 们时刻关心客户，并竭尽全力为他们服务。这也让 Rainmaker 们有更多时间更好地准备接下来的双向通话。

Voice-mail records the time and date of a call. Calls made at 6:15 A.M. and 11:10 P.M. are notable. Your customer will take note and remember.

语音信箱会记录通话的时间和日期。早上 6:15 和晚上 11:10 的通话都会被记录下来。您的客户会记录下来并记住。

# ↩

• 22 •

• 22 •

Learn the “Miles Per Gallon” of Selling

了解销售的“每加仑英里数”

S elling is a timed journey. The seller’s destination is usually a quota, a goal, a necessary amount of revenue. The timing of the journey is often a fiscal year, a deadline to bring in revenue (e.g., to meet next month’s payroll), or the sales cycle of the product.

销售是一段有时间限制的旅程。销售人员的目的地通常是配额、目标或必要的收入。旅程的时间通常是财政年度、收入截止日期（例如，支付下个月的工资）或产品的销售周期。

This timed journey is like an automobile trip. The length of the auto trip is the number of miles between the start and the arrival. The sales journey is the dollar revenue to generate from the beginning of the selling period to the end.

这个定时旅程就像一次汽车旅行。汽车行程的长度是指从出发地到目的地之间的里程数。销售旅程是指从销售期开始到结束所产生的美元收入。

The gas tank is the seller’s available number of sales calls. The miles per gallon is the seller’s call-to-close ratio. If the car has 25 gallons of gas, and gets 20 miles per gallon, the car can travel 500 miles. If the seller has 300 available sales calls in a year (number of selling days times average number of calls per day), and has a call-to-close ratio of 20:1 * (i.e., 20 calls for every sale), the salesperson can make 15 sales. If the seller, in this example, cannot increase the total available sales calls, or improve his call-to-close ratio, then the sales potential is fifteen closes… not sixteen.

油箱油量代表销售人员可拨打的销售电话数量。每加仑行驶的英里数代表销售人员的销售电话成交率。如果汽车有25加仑汽油，每加仑行驶20英里，那么这辆车可以行驶500英里。如果销售人员一年有300个可拨打的销售电话（销售天数乘以平均每日电话数量），并且销售电话成交率为20:1 * （即每笔销售对应20个电话），那么销售人员可以完成15笔销售。在本例中，如果销售人员无法增加可拨打的销售电话总数，或提高销售电话成交率，那么销售潜力就是15笔成交……而不是16笔。

The Rainmaker understands this mathematical reality. Consequently, this Rainmaker plans up to twenty calls on a target customer, and does not call on more than fifteen targets.

雨人深谙这一数学原理。因此，这位雨人会计划对每个目标客户进行最多20次拜访，但不会拜访超过15个目标客户。

The Rainmaker fishes where the big fish are. This means the Rainmaker calls on customers with large enough sales potential that, if closed, the resultant revenues will hit goal.

雨人会在大鱼所在的地方钓鱼。这意味着雨人会主动联系那些拥有足够大销售潜力的客户，一旦成交，最终的收入就能达到目标。

Less than 5 percent of all salespeople (and of all selling organizations) understand this concept intellectually, know how to calculate the math, know how to prioritize the probabilities, or have the discipline of the Rainmaker. Ninety-five percent of all salespeople will dilute themselves, by calling on too many customers and not allocating enough sales calls to close each sale. They will, in effect, run out of gas and not hit their goal.

在所有销售人员（以及所有销售组织中）中，只有不到5%的人能够理解这个概念，懂得如何计算，知道如何优先考虑各种可能性，或者拥有“雨人”般的自律。95%的销售人员会因为拜访过多的客户，而没有分配足够的销售电话来完成每笔交易，从而稀释自己的能量。实际上，他们会精疲力竭，无法达成目标。

Your available number of sales calls is your gas tank, your selling capital. If a home builder needs a mortgage of $140,000 to complete the house, and his banker only lends $130,000, what should the builder do, leave off the roof? It is better to lend $141,000 than $139,000. It is the same with selling. If it takes ten sales calls to close, don’t plan eight. If it takes ten calls to make the sale, then it is better to make no calls than to make nine.

你可用的销售电话数量就像你的油箱，你的销售资本。如果一个房屋建筑商需要14万美元的抵押贷款才能完成房屋建造，而他的银行只提供13万美元的贷款，那么建筑商该怎么办？把屋顶拆掉吗？贷款14.1万美元总比贷款13.9万美元好。销售也是如此。如果成交需要10个销售电话，就不要计划8个。如果成交需要10个电话，那么最好不打任何电话，而不是打9个电话。

In the art and painting business, it once took 14 sales calls to get a collector to invest in a museum piece. Therefore, the call-to-close ratio was 14:1. If the art salesperson made 130 calls on 10 collectors, a 13:1 ratio, he would make zero sales. But if the salesperson called 14 times on 9 accounts, a 14:1 ratio, he makes 9 sales.

在艺术和绘画行业，曾经需要打14个销售电话才能让一位收藏家投资一件博物馆藏品。因此，销售电话成交率为14:1。如果这位艺术品销售人员给10位收藏家打了130个电话，也就是13:1的比率，那么他的销售额为零。但如果这位销售人员给9个客户打了14个电话，也就是14:1的比率，那么他就能完成9笔交易。

You must determine how many sales calls—or gallons of gas—you have in your tank. You must maximize your miles per gallon, your call-to-close ratio.

你必须确定你的油箱里有多少个销售电话，或者说有多少加仑汽油。你必须最大限度地提高每加仑行驶里程，也就是你的销售电话成交率。

Work the math and the numbers will work for you.

进行数学计算，数字就会为你提供帮助。

Rainmakers don’t plan a thirty-mile trip with twenty miles’ worth of gas.

造雨者不会用二十英里的汽油来计划三十英里的旅程。

• 23 •

• 23 •

Beware the Myth of Time and Territory Management

警惕时间和领土管理的迷思

T here are books on how salespeople can optimize their time and territory management. There are sales courses given every day that show a salesperson how to get from here to there in the least amount of time. There are speakers roaming the countryside lecturing on how a salesperson can best cover all the accounts in the territory.

有很多书籍教销售人员如何优化时间和区域管理。每天都有销售课程，教销售人员如何用最短的时间完成工作。还有演讲者走遍乡村，讲解销售人员如何才能最好地覆盖区域内的所有客户。

Improving time and territory (T&T) management is an example of doing the wrong thing right. Time and territory management is an archaic concept relevant for both door-to-door and route salespeople. Its relevance today is as a productivity tool used superbly by companies such as UPS and FedEx.

改进时间和区域（T&T）管理就是把错误的事情做对的一个例子。时间和区域管理是一个古老的概念，对上门推销员和路线推销员都适用。如今，它作为一种生产力工具，被UPS和FedEx等公司出色地运用。

Time and territory management misdirects salespeople. The notion makes salespeople—and sales managers—believe that it is somehow wrong not to call on every good potential account in a territory. T&T sends too many salespeople to too many accounts, resulting in too few accounts receiving the optimal number of calls to result in new closes.

时间和区域管理误导了销售人员。这种观念让销售人员——以及销售经理——认为不拜访区域内所有优质潜在客户是错误的。大通公司（T&T）向过多的客户派出了过多的销售人员，导致只有极少数客户接到了最佳拜访次数，从而无法达成新的交易。

Adherence to exacting T&T methods is a socially acceptable excuse for not hitting quota. Interview a sales force and you will inevitably hear salespeople complain, “My territory is too big.”

严格遵守销售与服务（T&T）方法，是社会普遍接受的未完成配额的借口。采访销售人员时，你难免会听到销售人员抱怨：“我的销售区域太大了。”

How can it be a problem that a territory is “too big”? A real problem is if a territory, as measured in potential, is too small!

领土“太大”怎么会是个问题呢？真正的问题是，如果领土的潜力太小！

No one gets fired who brings in the business… regardless of how many accounts they call on. But lots of people get fired if they don’t ring the cash register, despite working hard and dutifully calling on every account.

无论拜访多少客户，带来业务的人都不会被解雇。但很多人即使努力工作，尽职尽责地拜访每一个客户，只要没有带来收入，就会被解雇。

Rainmakers concentrate their calls on the highest potential accounts. Making 100 percent of your calls on one make-the-quota account is perfect T&T management.

雨人会把电话集中在那些潜力最大的客户身上。把所有电话都打给一个达到配额要求的客户，才是完美的T&T管理。

Always Taste the Wine Before a Wine Tasting

品酒前务必先品尝葡萄酒

T his is a lesson on planning to prevent failure.

这是关于制定计划以防止失败的教训。

A wine tasting is a marketing event that wineries use to sell wines. A wine tasting is when people influential to the sale of wine—retailers, wine writers, restaurateurs—sample the product. Often the featured wine is a new one, or representative of a vintage just coming to market, or the first release from a new winery. If the wine tastes good, the influential tasters will be influenced to buy the wine or promote the winery.

品酒会是酒庄用来销售葡萄酒的营销活动。品酒会是指那些对葡萄酒销售有影响力的人士——零售商、葡萄酒作家、餐馆老板——品尝葡萄酒。通常，主打的葡萄酒是新品，或是刚上市的年份代表酒款，或是新酒庄的首发酒款。如果葡萄酒口感良好，这些有影响力的品酒者就会被吸引购买或推广酒庄。

Imagine the scene: The winemaker opens a bottle and pours an ounce or two into the glasses of ten wine magazine writers. To everyone’s dismay, the wine is bitter. As the winemaker scrambles to open another bottle, the writers scribble. The second bottle of wine is fine, as are the next one thousand, but the damage is done.

想象一下这样的场景：酿酒师打开一瓶酒，往十位葡萄酒杂志撰稿人的酒杯里倒了一两盎司的酒。令所有人失望的是，这酒竟然苦涩难闻。酿酒师手忙脚乱地打开另一瓶酒，而撰稿人则在一旁草草地记着。第二瓶酒没问题，接下来的一千瓶也没问题，但损失已经造成了。

Never assume something you can check. Pay attention to the details. Roll up your sleeves and get your hands dirty. If the project is important, every single detail is important. Broadway plays are exhaustively rehearsed. Experienced pilots always complete a comprehensive preflight checklist. Always check the laptop connections and power sources before making a presentation. Always check the microphone before giving a speech. Before you show your e-commerce website to a potential investor, be sure it works. Always precall plan a sales call.

永远不要想当然地认为可以检查的事情。关注细节。卷起袖子，亲自动手。如果项目很重要，那么每一个细节都至关重要。百老汇戏剧的排练都经过了详尽的准备。经验丰富的飞行员总是会完成一份全面的飞行前检查清单。在做演示之前，务必检查笔记本电脑的连接和电源。在发表演讲之前，务必检查麦克风。在向潜在投资者展示你的电商网站之前，务必确保它能够正常运行。务必提前计划一次销售拜访。

A successful criminal attorney is called the “Furniture Mover” by bailiffs and other court personnel. This attorney leaves nothing he can control to chance. Before each trial, he visits the courtroom and, depending on his strategy, moves his client’s chair closer to or farther from the jury. He places tables in the sunlight or the shade. He speaks aloud, checking the acoustics. He is tasting the wine. Unlike the hapless winemaker, when the Furniture Mover opens his case, his jury savors the product.

一位成功的刑事律师被法警和其他法庭工作人员称为“家具搬运工”。这位律师不会放过任何他能掌控的事情。每次开庭前，他都会前往法庭，根据自己的策略，将客户的座位移近或移远陪审团。他会把桌子摆放在阳光下或阴凉处。他会大声说话，检查音响效果。他还会品尝葡萄酒。与倒霉的酿酒师不同，当“家具搬运工”打开案卷时，陪审团会细细品味。

Rainmakers always test in private what they are going to sell in public.

Rainmakers 总是会私下测试他们准备公开销售的产品。

Dare to Be Dumb

敢于犯傻

T he biggest criticism of salespeople by customers is that salespeople don’t ask enough questions. Preplanned, practiced questions are arrows in the salesperson’s quiver. Good questions get the customer talking, elicit information, allow the salesperson to listen, and demonstrate to the customers the salesperson’s genuine interest. If you don’t do a proper diagnosis, you won’t have the correct prescription. Asking too few questions is asking to fail. Hearken to the hotshot criminal detective who related her biggest fear while conducting an investigation: “I am always afraid I will not ask the one important question that unlocks the case.”

客户对销售人员最大的批评就是问的问题不够多。事先计划好、练习过的问题就像销售人员的利箭。好的问题能引发客户的谈话，引出信息，让销售人员认真倾听，并向客户展现销售人员真正的兴趣。如果没有正确的诊断，就无法开出正确的药方。问得太少就等于自取灭亡。听听那位出色的刑事侦探讲述她在调查过程中最大的恐惧：“我总是担心自己问不出那个能解开案情的关键问题。”

There are a number of reasons why too many salespeople ask too few questions. Ineffective salespeople don’t prepare enough questions in precall. They don’t write the questions down. They mistakenly think questioning is intrusive, impertinent. Ineffective salespeople assume they already know the answers. Some actually do know the answers, but that’s irrelevant. And some salespeople are afraid that asking questions will diminish them, make them appear less expert.

很多销售人员提问过少，原因有很多。低效的销售人员在销售前准备的问题不够充分。他们没有把问题写下来。他们错误地认为提问是无礼的、不恰当的。低效的销售人员以为自己已经知道答案。有些人确实知道答案，但这并不重要。有些销售人员担心提问会降低他们的专业水平，让他们显得不够专业。

All of these reasons are misguided and unacceptable. Customers love questions. Customers love to talk. Customers feel more secure with the salesperson who asks questions and listens and takes notes.

所有这些理由都是误导性的，不可接受的。顾客喜欢提问，喜欢交流。顾客对那些主动提问、认真倾听并做笔记的销售人员更有信心。

To the concerned customer with a need there is no such thing as a dumb question. So dare to be dumb. Assume nothing. Even if you have the perfect feel for a problem, ask questions so that the customer will know you understand.

对于有需求的客户来说，没有什么问题是愚蠢的。所以，勇敢地尝试愚蠢的想法。不要想当然。即使你对问题有敏锐的洞察力，也要提出问题，让客户知道你理解。

Year after year, the top salesman for an adhesive company is a guy they call Columbo (after the television character). This Rainmaker has two degrees in engineering, plus a post grad in mechanical engineering. He knows how things are made. He can take apart anything and put it back together. He knows springs, fasteners, seals, valves, blueprints, machinery.

年复一年，一家粘合剂公司的顶级销售员总是被一个叫哥伦布（Columbo，取自电视剧中的角色）的人占据。这位“雨人”拥有两个工程学位，外加一个机械工程研究生学位。他深谙万物制造之道。他能拆开任何东西，再重新组装起来。他精通弹簧、紧固件、密封件、阀门、图纸和机械设备。

Despite his years of experience and ability to instantly sort out a problem, he asks what his colleagues think are dumb questions:

尽管他拥有多年的经验，并且能够立即解决问题，但他还是会问同事们认为很愚蠢的问题：

• “How do you make this part?”

• “您是如何制作这个部件的？”

• “Why do you make it this way?”

• “你为什么要这样做？”

• “How do you assemble the part?”

• “如何组装该部件？”

• “Why do you put that bolt there?”

• “你为什么把螺栓放在那里？”

• “How much do the bolts cost you?”

• “这些螺栓多少钱？”

• “If you could eliminate one bolt per assembly with a less expensive method, that would save you money, correct?”

• “如果您能用更便宜的方法减少每个组件中的一个螺栓，那就能省钱，对吗？”

• “If I can show you how to fasten the assembly as well as it’s fastened now, but with less cost to you, would you be interested?”

• “如果我可以向您展示如何像现在这样很好地固定组件，但成本更低，您会感兴趣吗？”

And so on to a close.

如此反复直至结束。

Customers don’t care how technically smart you are. They expect your product to work. And if the product or solution is new to them, they will usually require a test before purchasing. Customers care about outcomes, not the intricacies of your technology.

客户不在乎你的技术有多高超。他们希望你的产品能够正常工作。如果产品或解决方案对他们来说是全新的，他们通常会在购买前进行测试。客户关心的是结果，而不是你技术的复杂性。

Rainmakers ask “dumb” questions and become the highest paid salespeople in their companies.

造雨人会问“愚蠢”的问题，并成为公司中薪酬最高的销售人员。

Thus, if you are a lock salesperson calling on a university interested in new electronic safety card keys, it is perfectly all right, in fact mandatory, to ask the decision makers, “Why do you want a lock?” The president of the university, and the head of maintenance, and the director of admissions, and the head of security, and so on, will each give you a different answer. And each answer will express a need for which the Rainmaker will then dollarize.

因此，如果你是一名锁具销售员，拜访一所对新型电子安全卡钥匙感兴趣的大学，你完全可以，甚至必须问他们的决策者：“你们为什么想要锁？” 校长、维护主管、招生主任、安保主管等等，每个人都会给你不同的答案。而每个答案都表达了一种需求，而“雨人”会将这种需求转化为金钱。

Always Do an Investment Return Analysis

始终进行投资回报分析

T he investment return analysis is a powerful selling tool designed to get new customers and new applications. The investment return analysis calculates the economic benefits your customer will get from using your solution.

投资回报分析是一个强大的销售工具，旨在帮助您获得新客户和新应用。它计算客户使用您的解决方案将获得的经济效益。

If you had two equal risk investment options, one returning 5 percent and the other 10 percent, where would you invest your money?

如果您有两个同等风险的投资选择，一个回报率为 5%，另一个回报率为 10%，您会将钱投资在哪里？

The concept of return on investment is simple, and it is the basis for nearly every business purchase decision. The Rainmaker knows this and uses arithmetic to show the customer how a $2,000 investment in a lathe will save $1,200 a year in reduced scrap. The reduced scrap is the benefit. The $1,200 is the dollarization of that benefit. In this scenario the customer gets a 60 percent per annum return on investment.

投资回报率的概念很简单，它几乎是所有商业采购决策的基础。Rainmaker 深谙此道，并用数学方法向客户展示，投资 2,000 美元购买一台车床，每年可以减少 1,200 美元的废品。减少的废品就是收益，而 1,200 美元则是这笔收益的美元化体现。在这种情况下，客户每年可获得 60% 的投资回报率。

The greater the customer’s return on investment, the more compelling it is for the customer to purchase—that is, make the investment. A properly calculated investment return analysis shows the customer what it is costing per day to go without the solution. In the lathe example, the customer gets $1,200 in savings returned. It is costing the customer $100 a month not to buy the lathe.

客户的投资回报率越高，就越能吸引客户购买，也就是进行投资。经过合理计算的投资回报率分析，可以向客户展示不使用解决方案每天的成本。以车床为例，客户节省了 1,200 美元。如果不购买车床，客户每月将损失 100 美元。

Showing the customer what it costs per month, week, or day to go without the solution shortens the sales cycle.

向客户展示不使用解决方案每月、每周或每天的成本可以缩短销售周期。

The investment return analysis helps your customer sell your solution inside his organization. There are usually eight to twelve hidden decision makers who need to say yes. Whether you are selling a pharmaceutical centrifuge for $500,000 or a stainless-steel bolt for $.05, your customer will need to justify the decision to go with your products. Your customer contact will use the investment return analysis to convince his or her colleagues.

投资回报分析有助于您的客户在其组织内部推销您的解决方案。通常有八到十二个隐藏的决策者需要同意。无论您出售的是价值 50 万美元的制药离心机，还是价值 0.05 美元的不锈钢螺栓，您的客户都需要证明选择您产品的决策是合理的。您的客户联系人将使用投资回报分析来说服他的同事。

The Rainmaker uses the investment return analysis to show the true cost (versus price) of the product. The Rainmaker doesn’t sell the product. The Rainmaker sells what the customer will get from the product. The Rainmaker doesn’t sell drills, he sells holes… and holes that are $.02 less expensive to drill.

Rainmaker 使用投资回报分析来显示产品的真实成本（相对于价格）。Rainmaker 不销售产品本身，而是销售客户从产品中获得的收益。Rainmaker 不销售钻头，而是销售孔……而且是比原价便宜 0.02 美元的孔。

Never Forget: Everybody Is Somebody’s Somebody

永远不要忘记：每个人都是别人的某个人

I t was a typical diner. There was a counter, booths, and tables. The menu, a collage of pictures of sandwiches and sundaes, was laminated. The prices were reasonable. The wait-staff included a bunch of summer-job high school kids. The restaurant was in an affluent area.

这是一家典型的小餐馆。有柜台、卡座和桌子。菜单是三明治和圣代的拼贴画，用过塑封过。价格合理。服务员包括一群做暑期工的高中生。这家餐馆位于一个富裕的地区。

One customer was upset about something. He was angry with one of the young waitresses. He was loud, rude, and nasty. Perhaps she had made an error on the bill, or there was not enough B in his BLT? Whatever it was, his overreaction brought tears to the teenager’s eyes. The guy finally threw some money down and stomped out.

一位顾客因为某事不高兴。他对一位年轻的女服务员很生气。那位服务员又吵又粗鲁，语气也很恶劣。也许是服务员记错了账单，又或者是他的培根生菜番茄三明治（BLT）里的培根生菜番茄三明治（BLT）不够？不管是什么原因，他过度的反应让这位青少年哭了起来。最后，那位服务员扔下一些钱，气冲冲地走了。

Three other kids watched what happened. One of the two boys behind the counter said, “I know that guy. I’ve seen him in my father’s office.”

另外三个孩子看着这一幕。柜台后面的一个男孩说：“我认识那家伙。我在我爸爸的办公室里见过他。”

Remarkably, each of the four high school kids had a parent who was a doctor. They found out from the boy’s father that the angry customer was a salesman for a pharmaceutical company. Then and there, each kid planned to tell their parents not to do business with that salesman.

值得注意的是，这四个高中生的父母都是医生。他们从男孩的父亲那里得知，那位愤怒的顾客是一家制药公司的销售员。当时，每个孩子都计划告诉父母，不要和那个销售员做生意。

Being nice to somebody’s somebody may not get you a client. But being hurtful to somebody’s somebody could hurt you.

对某人的某人好，你可能不会得到客户。但伤害某人的某人，却可能伤害到你。

Rainmakers make friends, not enemies.

祈雨者结交朋友，而不是树敌。

Always Be on “High Receive”

始终保持“高接收”状态

Y our job is to listen to your customer. You must accurately hear what they are saying and not saying. You must be acutely aware of all verbal and nonverbal signals. You must find out what the customer wants, needs, and doesn’t want. You must learn how and when you can help the customer.

你的工作是倾听客户。你必须准确地听出他们所说的和未说的内容。你必须敏锐地察觉所有言语和非言语信号。你必须了解客户想要什么、需要什么以及不想要什么。你必须学会如何以及何时能够帮助客户。

To do this you must watch and listen to your customer as sensitively and intently as military spy equipment monitors enemy movements and communication. Like the most sensitive of receptors you must be on high receive. Let nothing get by you; even the casual, offhand remark may offer clues.

要做到这一点，你必须敏锐而专注地观察和倾听客户，就像军用间谍设备监视敌人的动向和通信一样。如同最敏感的接收器一样，你必须保持高度接收。不要错过任何细节；即使是漫不经心、随口说出的话也可能提供线索。

Ask interesting questions. Listen carefully. Don’t daydream. Don’t mentally wander when the customer is telling you something you’ve heard a hundred times before. Don’t start talking until the customer has completely stopped talking. Don’t think about what you are going to say next. Take notes.

提出有趣的问题。认真倾听。不要心不在焉。当顾客说一些你听过无数遍的话时，不要走神。在顾客完全停止说话之前，不要开口。不要思考接下来要说什么。做好笔记。

Turn off all smartphones, tablets, and other electronic devices before you meet with a customer. A ringing cell phone, hiding in a briefcase or a pocket, is an annoyance, is discourteous, and breaks concentration. Don’t let the customer see you carrying a mobile device.

与客户见面前，请关闭所有智能手机、平板电脑和其他电子设备。手机铃声响起，藏在公文包或口袋里，会令人烦恼，不礼貌，还会分散注意力。不要让客户看到你携带移动设备。

A woman was interviewing companies to remodel her bathrooms. She had carefully written down her decorating goals. She wanted to be sure the contractor she chose heard her idea, could offer suggestions, had the time to do the job, and would be affordable. The contractors she called were recommended by reliable references.

一位女士正在面试几家公司来翻新她的浴室。她仔细地写下了自己的装修目标。她希望确保自己选择的承包商能够听取她的想法，能够提供建议，有时间完成工作，并且价格合理。她联系的承包商都是可靠的推荐人推荐的。

Each contractor arrived on time, took notes, asked questions. During a discussion of tile colors and sizes, one of the contractors’ phones rang. He immediately moved to an outer room to take the call or text a response. Minutes later he was back to the bathroom.

每位承包商都准时到达，做笔记，提出问题。在讨论瓷砖颜色和尺寸时，一位承包商的电话响了。他立即转移到外面的房间接电话或发短信回复。几分钟后，他又回到了浴室。

Two days later both contractors e-mailed their plan, schedule, and bid. The ringing–cell phone contractor’s bid was the lowest by $1,500. The woman chose the higher bidder. She explained her choice: “Both companies were good. But if a call from the office is more important than my time, then why would I do business with them? I should be the highest priority when I hire someone.”

两天后，两家承包商都通过电子邮件发送了他们的计划、日程安排和报价。响铃手机承包商的报价最低，低了1500美元。这位女士选择了出价更高的那家。她解释了她的选择：“两家公司都不错。但如果办公室打来的电话比我的时间更重要，那我为什么要和他们做生意？我雇人的时候应该优先考虑我。”

The three most important words in the Rainmaker’s mind are “listen, listen, listen,” and to do so on “high receive.”

在 Rainmaker 心中，最重要的三个词是“听，听，听”，以及“高接收”。

Rainmakers focus on the customers. Rainmakers give individual attention. To the Rainmaker the customer is king, and the sales call is an invitation to the king’s court.

雨人专注于客户。雨人给予个性化关注。对雨人而言，客户就是上帝，而销售拜访则是通往国王宫廷的邀请。

“Onionize”

“洋葱化”

T o be successful, the Rainmaker must first get to the essence, the core, of what the customer needs. The Rainmaker must find the problem. The Rainmaker must understand all of the customer’s concerns, desires, fears, and limits. The Rainmaker cannot prescribe until he or she diagnoses. The Rainmaker cannot turn the customer’s need into a want until he or she knows how to put value on the customer’s desired state. Just as a sous chef peels an onion layer by layer, so, too, the Rainmaker helps the customer get to the “heart of the matter.”

要想成功，雨人首先必须抓住客户需求的本质和核心。雨人必须找到问题所在。雨人必须了解客户所有的顾虑、渴望、恐惧和局限。雨人只有在诊断清楚后才能开药。雨人只有在懂得如何赋予客户期望状态价值后才能将客户的需求转化为渴望。正如副厨师一层一层地剥洋葱一样，雨人也需要帮助客户触及“问题的核心”。

Rainmakers use the word onionize as a memory trigger to remind themselves to keep probing, to keep asking questions, especially “why,” “why,” “why,” and “why.”

造雨者使用“洋葱化”这个词作为记忆触发器，提醒自己不断探索，不断提问，尤其是“为什么”、“为什么”、“为什么”和“为什么”。

This is how a Rainmaker onionizes the customer:

Rainmaker 是这样将客户“洋葱化”的：

“Tell me how the current situation is worrisome to you.”

“告诉我目前的情况让你担心的是什么。”

“Why is that important to you?”

“这对你来说为什么重要？”

“How is that important to you?”

“这对你来说有什么重要意义？”

“What are the consequences if this continues unimproved?”

“如果这种情况继续下去，会有什么后果？”

“Can we try to find a solution that costs less than the problem?”

“我们能否尝试找到一个成本低于问题的解决方案？”

“How often does the machine go down or stop working?”

“机器多久会出现一次故障或停止工作？”

“What is the failure mode?”

“故障模式是什么？”

“Why do you think that?”

“你为什么这么想？”

“So the present seal occasionally loses its tolerance and then leaks, correct?”

“所以现在的封印偶尔会失去耐受力，然后泄漏，对吗？”

“If you could get a new seal design that would eliminate leaks, would that be an answer?”

“如果你能找到一种可以消除泄漏的新型密封设计，那就算答案了吗？”

“Here’s your new seal. If, after testing, it works as promised, is there any other reason prohibiting you from recommending it for full production?”

“这是您的新印章。如果测试后，它确实像承诺的那样有效，还有其他原因阻止您推荐它投入全面生产吗？”

And fifty other onionizing questions are interspersed.

其中还穿插了五十个其他令人困惑的问题。

Rainmakers are akin to investigative reporters, detectives, psychiatrists, doctors, and archaeologists. They ask, probe, dig, diagnose, and listen. Rainmakers onionize to understand.

造雨人类似于调查记者、侦探、精神病学家、医生和考古学家。他们询问、探索、挖掘、诊断、倾听。造雨人将洋葱化，以便理解。

If You Don’t Care About the Answer, Don’t Ask the Question

如果你不在乎答案，就不要问这个问题

T his is about sincerity.

这关乎诚意。

If you don’t really want to hear all about every shot the customer took on her recent golf vacation to St. Andrews, Scotland, then don’t ask. If you don’t really give a hoot about the brilliant babblings of his new baby, then don’t ask. If the customer’s bronzed rugby shoes are not relevant to the sale, don’t ask about them. Don’t waste precious selling time—yours and your customer’s—on matters not pertinent to helping your customer improve his or her situation.

如果你真的不想听顾客最近去苏格兰圣安德鲁斯打高尔夫度假时的每一杆击球，那就别问。如果你真的不在乎他新宝宝的妙语连珠，那就别问。如果顾客的古铜色橄榄球鞋与销售无关，就别问。不要把宝贵的销售时间——你和顾客的——浪费在与帮助顾客改善自身状况无关的事情上。

If you ask about the picture of the sailboat, you may get an answer. And that answer will include every tack, every wind shift, every storm from San Diego to Fiji. And the customer will deliberately or unconsciously scuttle the call. Unless you are selling sailcloth, ask about the sailboat on your way out.

如果你询问帆船的照片，你可能会得到答案。答案里会包含从圣地亚哥到斐济的每一次航行、每一次风向变化、每一次风暴。顾客可能会有意无意地取消电话。除非你卖的是帆布，否则出门前最好问问帆船的情况。

Rainmakers don’t squander sales calls with unnecessary chitchat or entertaining conversation. Rainmakers are nice, engaging, informed, interesting, and interested… and always sincere.

雨人不会在销售电话中浪费时间，不会在无聊的闲聊或娱乐性谈话中浪费时间。雨人友善、迷人、见多识广、风趣幽默、充满热情……而且总是真诚待人。

Asking a question to flatter the customer is a form of insincerity, and is usually transparent to the customer. Customers are more impressed by intelligent, legitimate get-to-the-problem questions than they are by a phony inquiry.

为了讨好顾客而提问其实是一种不真诚的表现，顾客通常一眼就能看出来。相比虚假的询问，聪明、合理、切中要害的问题更能打动顾客。
