Never Be in a Meeting

永远不要参加会议

W hen a customer calls, they don’t want to hear that you are in a meeting. Customers don’t care if you are meeting with the president of the United States, the pope, or anyone else. Customers absolutely lose it when told you are meeting with others in your company. Customers don’t care with whom you are meeting—with one exception: It is OK if you are meeting with another customer. It’s OK because being with customers, and taking care of customers, is what you and everyone else in your company is supposed to do.

当客户打电话时，他们不想听到你正在开会。客户不在乎你正在和美国总统、教皇还是其他任何人开会。当客户被告知你正在和公司其他人开会时，他们绝对会失控。客户不在乎你和谁开会——但有一个例外：如果你正在和另一个客户开会，那就没问题。这没问题，因为陪伴客户、照顾客户，是你和公司里其他人应该做的。

If you are in a company meeting and a customer calls, always take the call. A customer call is an invitation to help the customer, to get or keep his or her business.

如果您正在公司开会，接到客户的电话，请务必接听。客户来电是邀请您提供帮助，争取或留住客户的邀请。

In addition to never being in a meeting, you are also never sick. You are traveling.

你除了不用开会之外，也从来不会生病。你只是在旅行。

You are never on vacation. You are traveling, or out of the country, and will return calls as soon as possible. Meanwhile, so-and-so is available to work with the customer.

您永远不会休假。您正在旅行或出国，并且会尽快回电。与此同时，某某可以与客户沟通。

You have never “left for the day.” You are out of the office or meeting with customers.

你从来没有“离开一天”。你只是离开了办公室或者去见客户了。

You are never “out to lunch.” You are meeting with a client.

你永远不会“出去吃午饭”。你正在和客户见面。

You are never “not in the office yet.” You are at a breakfast meeting with a client.

你永远不会“还没到办公室”。你正在和客户开早餐会。

If the Rainmaker is temporarily unavailable, the customer knows where she is. The Rainmaker is not “in a meeting,” she is in court, on a job site, traveling to a customer, on a photo shoot, giving a talk at a convention, doing research…

如果“雨人”暂时不在，客户也能知道她在哪里。“雨人”不是在“开会”，而是在法庭上、在工地上、在拜访客户、在拍摄照片、在会议上演讲、在做研究……

Present for Show, Close for Dough

为表演而呈现，为赚钱而结束

I n golf, they say “drive for show, putt for dough.” The idea is that huge smashing three-hundred-yard drives are less important than making a six-foot putt. A drive can land left or right in the fairway, or fifty yards short, and have less impact on the golfer’s score than a putt two inches to the left or one inch short. Putting is unforgiving. A one-inch putt is equal to a one-hundred-yard shot. The professional golfers who make the most money are the best putters.

高尔夫界有句俗语：“开球作秀，推杆赚大钱”。意思是，一记300码的大力开球远不如一记6英尺的推杆重要。一记开球可能落在球道左侧或右侧，也可能落在球道右侧50码，对球手成绩的影响远不及一记向左偏两英寸或向右偏一英寸的推杆。推杆是无可厚非的。一英寸的推杆相当于一记100码的击球。赚最多钱的职业高尔夫球手，往往都是推杆高手。

In selling, it is “present for show, close for dough.” Don’t depend on a fancy audiovisual or PowerPoint presentation to get the sale. Don’t assume that giving a customer a colorful brochure is selling. Most customers don’t say, “That video was so good I have to buy immediately.”

销售的精髓在于“做秀，成交才有回报”。不要依赖华丽的视听材料或PowerPoint演示文稿来促成销售。不要以为给顾客一份色彩鲜艳的宣传册就能卖出好价钱。大多数顾客不会说：“那个视频太棒了，我得马上买。”

Presentations, demonstrations, and engaging trade-show booths are a waste of money if they are not accompanied by a practiced, proactive strategy to get the customer to buy.

如果没有采取成熟、积极主动的策略来吸引客户购买，那么演示、示范和引人入胜的贸易展览摊位就只是浪费金钱。

To some salespeople, a well-produced presentation is a crutch; to a Rainmaker, it is a tool. Some salespeople present and hope the customer decides to say yes. The Rainmaker presents and helps the customer to decide.

对一些销售人员来说，精心制作的演示文稿是拐杖；而对“雨人”来说，它是一种工具。一些销售人员演示，希望客户决定答应。而“雨人”则演示，帮助客户做出决定。

Rainmakers are cool and calm, and they don’t miss many three-foot putts.

雨人冷静沉着，他们不会错过很多三英尺推杆。

Advice to a Baby-sitter

给保姆的建议

B aby-sitting—for pay—is a noble job, a noble profession. Baby-sitters look after their clients’ most precious possession. Baby-sitters are teenage kids, au pairs, nannies, and day care centers.

照顾婴儿——有偿的——是一项高尚的工作，一份高尚的职业。保姆照顾着客户最珍贵的宝贝。保姆可以是青少年、互惠生、保育员，也可以是日托中心的工作人员。

In general, baby-sitters are in business for themselves. They get the jobs, do the work, and get paid. If they do a good job, they are rehired. As in many professions, excellent baby-sitters get paid more than the run-of-the-mill baby-sitter.

一般来说，保姆是自己做生意。他们得到工作，做好工作，然后获得报酬。如果他们做得好，就会被重新聘用。和许多职业一样，优秀的保姆比普通的保姆收入更高。

A teenage girl was getting ready for her first baby-sitting job with a new family, a new client. The teenager was ambitious, conscientious, and wanted spending money. The girl’s mother asked her daughter if she would like some marketing advice about baby-sitting.

一位十几岁的女孩正准备迎接她的第一份保姆工作，她要照顾一个新家庭和一位新客户。这位少女雄心勃勃、认真负责，而且想要一些零花钱。女孩的母亲问女儿是否想听听一些关于保姆的营销建议。

This appealed to the business-minded baby-sitter.

这对有商业头脑的保姆很有吸引力。

The mother gave the girl two tips: “One, no matter how bad the kids are, no matter how much trouble they cause, when the parents come home and ask if there were any problems, you tell the parents ‘no problems, everything was fine.’ And, two, leave the house a little cleaner than you found it.”

母亲给了女孩两个建议：“第一，不管孩子有多坏，不管他们惹了多大的麻烦，当父母回家问有什么问题时，你要告诉父母‘没问题，一切都很好’。第二，离开时，房子要比你刚来的时候干净一点。”

This is great advice for the Rainmaker. Once a customer hires you to do a job, they don’t want to know your problems doing the job. They don’t care. Do a wonderful job, do it on time, do it on budget, don’t complain, and give the customer a little extra. This is the blueprint for customer satisfaction and for continued sales success.

这对“造雨人”来说是个很棒的建议。一旦客户雇佣你做某项工作，他们就不会想知道你在工作中遇到的问题。他们不在乎。要出色地完成工作，按时完成，在预算内完成，不要抱怨，并给客户一点额外的奖励。这是客户满意度和持续销售成功的蓝图。

The teenage girl is now a Baby-sitter Rainmaker. She sells a relaxed evening and a neat house. She is always in demand.

这位少女如今成了“雨人”的保姆。她带来的是轻松的夜晚和整洁的房子。她一直很抢手。

Killer Sales Question #4

杀手级销售问题 #4

C ustomers need to be convinced that your product or service will work as claimed. The greater the investment, the greater the need for the customer to be sure. The newer the technology, the greater the need to test. Anything new—product, supplier, salesperson—usually triggers the need for some kind of proof.

客户需要确信你的产品或服务能够像宣传的那样有效。投入越大，客户就越需要确信。技术越新，测试的需求就越大。任何新事物——产品、供应商、销售人员——通常都会引发某种形式的验证需求。

There are various ways customers get the proof they need: samples, small assignments, product evaluations, product trials, demonstrations, references, beta tests, test markets. Marketers of consumer package goods use samples, for example, to get customers to know the product. (Wrigley chewing gum was launched in its hometown of Chicago by sending a pack of gum to everyone in the phone book.) Companies selling to other companies often use product demonstrations to convince.

顾客获取所需证明的方式多种多样：样品、小型作业、产品评估、产品试用、演示、推荐、beta 测试、市场测试。例如，消费品包装的营销人员会使用样品来让顾客了解产品。（箭牌口香糖在其发源地芝加哥推出时，会向电话簿上的每个人寄送一包口香糖。）其他公司销售产品时，通常会使用产品演示来说服顾客。

Product demonstrations are often tricky to arrange. The salesperson must have the proper equipment, power supply, backup parts, recording sheets. Most important, the decision makers have to be present to view the demonstration.

产品演示的安排通常很棘手。销售人员必须配备合适的设备、电源、备用零件和记录表。最重要的是，决策者必须到场观看演示。

When a customer asks for a product demonstration, the Rainmaker responds as follows: “We would be happy to give you a demonstration. If the demo is successful, is there anything else prohibiting you from going ahead?”

当客户要求进行产品演示时，Rainmaker 会这样回复：“我们很乐意为您演示。如果演示成功，还有什么阻碍您继续进行吗？”

This is a killer sales question.

这是一个关键的销售问题。

By asking “Is there anything else prohibiting you…,” the salesperson is either going to hear some unresolved customer issues, or get an agreement to an action that leads to a close.

通过询问“还有其他什么禁止您……”，销售人员要么会听到一些未解决的客户问题，要么会获得达成交易的行动协议。

Rainmakers never leave product samples if the samples must somehow be tested. The Rainmaker knows that 95 percent of all samples left to be tested are still in a drawer or were tested incorrectly. The Rainmaker is always present when the customer tests the product.

如果样品必须进行测试，Rainmaker 绝不会留下任何样品。Rainmaker 深知，95% 的待测样品仍在抽屉中或测试不当。客户测试产品时，Rainmaker 始终在场。

Rainmakers never do a test or demo without first getting an agreement from the customers to go ahead with the sale if the test is successful.

Rainmakers 绝不会在未获得客户同意（如果测试成功则不进行销售）的情况下进行测试或演示。

Rainmakers never let the customer do the demo in his or her absence. If the customer makes an error, the salesperson suffers.

Rainmakers 绝不会让客户在自己不在场的情况下进行演示。如果客户出错，销售人员就会承担损失。

Rainmakers get buying commitments before they give selling demonstrations.

创雨者在进行销售演示之前会获得购买承诺。

Give and Get

付出与收获

I n selling, if you give something, you should plan to get something in return from the customer. The customer knows you are a salesperson. The customer knows you are in business. The customer knows that you make your living by providing your product to solve, if possible, the customer’s problem. The customer is ethical (otherwise be careful). The customer wouldn’t be seeing you if you weren’t ethical. The honest customer knows that he or she can’t get something for nothing (even if their negotiations might suggest otherwise).

在销售中，如果你付出了，就应该计划从顾客那里得到回报。顾客知道你是一名销售人员。顾客知道你在做生意。顾客知道你通过提供产品（如果可能的话）来解决顾客的问题来谋生。顾客是有道德的（否则要小心）。如果你不讲道德，顾客就不会来看你了。诚实的顾客知道，他/她不可能不劳而获（即使他们的谈判可能表明并非如此）。

• If you give a sample, get an agreement to test.

• 如果您提供样品，请获得测试协议。

• If you give a product demonstration, first get an agreement to buy if the demo proves the product works as claimed.

• 如果您进行产品演示，请首先达成购买协议，前提是演示证明产品确实按照宣传的方式运行。

• If you give a brochure, get an appointment.

• 如果您提供小册子，请预约。

• If you give a discount, get more volume.

• 如果您给予折扣，则可以获得更多的销量。

• If you give a free drink, get a next dinner.

• 如果您赠送一杯免费饮料，即可获得下一顿晚餐。

• If you give a favor, get a due bill.

• 如果你给予了恩惠，就得到应有的报酬。

• If you give a solution, get paid.

• 如果您提供解决方案，我们将向您支付报酬。

David Ogilvy was the greatest copy writer in the history of advertising. Ogilvy was also an awesome Rainmaker: He brought in wonderful clients to his advertising agency. He was a master at giving and getting. One of David Ogilvy’s memorable advertising campaigns was a series of ads he wrote to promote his agency, Ogilvy & Mather, in New York City.

大卫·奥格威是广告史上最伟大的文案撰稿人。奥格威也是一位出色的“雨人”：他为自己的广告公司带来了众多优秀的客户。他是一位善于付出和收获的大师。大卫·奥格威最令人难忘的广告活动之一是他为推广其位于纽约市的奥美广告公司而撰写的一系列广告。

Unlike the typical, predictable, and egotistical advertising that most agencies produce to promote themselves, Ogilvy “gave” his genius away. Instead of telling potential clients how great O&M was, instead of writing about himself, Ogilvy gave away how to do what his agency did.

与大多数广告公司为了推销自己而制作的那种典型、千篇一律、自负的广告不同，奥格威“倾囊相授”了他的才华。他没有告诉潜在客户奥美广告公司有多么优秀，也没有写关于自己的文章，而是分享了公司是如何运作的。

One ad, headlined “How to Write a Corporate Ad,” gave an accurate, detailed road map on copy points, layout, typeface, mistakes to avoid. Another, headlined “How to Make a Television Commercial,” revealed Ogilvy’s approaches and secrets.

一则名为“如何撰写企业广告”的广告，提供了精准详细的路线图，涵盖了文案要点、版式、字体以及应避免的错误。另一则名为“如何制作电视广告”的广告，则揭示了奥美的制作方法和秘诀。

One can imagine the internal debate at O&M: “If we tell them how we do it, they won’t need us!” But the sage and savvy Rainmaker knew coffee companies made coffee not ads, and that automakers made cars not commercials. He figured potential clients would not go to his competitors and say, “Make me ads the way Ogilvy does it.”

可以想象奥美广告公司内部会争论不休：“如果我们告诉他们怎么做，他们就不需要我们了！” 但睿智精明的Rainmaker知道，咖啡公司做的是咖啡而不是广告，汽车制造商做的是汽车而不是广告。他认为潜在客户不会去找竞争对手说：“像奥美那样给我做广告吧。”

He knew that there is a huge difference between being shown how something is done, and then doing it at all, let alone well. If simply showing how to do something well were the answer, then simply watching Picasso paint or Roger Federer play tennis or Julia Child make a soufflé would make everyone experts on everything.

他知道，在被告知如何做某件事和真正做到，更不用说做好这件事之间，存在着巨大的差异。如果仅仅告诉别人如何做好某件事就能解决问题，那么仅仅看毕加索画画、罗杰·费德勒打网球或茱莉亚·查尔德做蛋奶酥，就能让每个人成为所有事情的专家。

Ogilvy’s ads “gave away” this special knowledge and expertise, and got clients.

奥美的广告“赠送”了这些特殊的知识和专业技能，并获得了客户。

The Rainmaker gives to get.

雨人通过付出来获得。

Sell on Friday Afternoons

周五下午出售

A ny time is a good time to make a sales call on a decision maker. Excellent selling times are before eight o’clock any morning and after three on Friday afternoons. Early-morning sales calls are good for two reasons: (1) there are fewer, or limited, interruptions, and (2) the customer’s agreement to the unusual hour is a big buy signal.

任何时候都是向决策者进行销售拜访的好时机。最佳销售时间是每天早上八点之前和周五下午三点之后。清晨销售拜访之所以好，有两个原因：(1) 干扰较少或有限；(2) 客户同意这个不寻常的时间是一个重要的购买信号。

Friday afternoon is a wonderful time to see customers. There are several compelling reasons for this. The customer is often more relaxed, more forthcoming, less harried, and less defensive. The customer is already thinking about a weekend at the beach or planting a garden. Some customers feel that if they make a decision on Friday, they can “sleep on it” over the weekend. To some customers, deciding to go ahead with your project provides a sense of accomplishment, gets something off the “to do” list.

周五下午是拜访客户的绝佳时机。这有几个令人信服的理由。客户通常更放松，更坦诚，不那么焦虑，防御心理也不那么强。他们已经在考虑周末去海滩度假或种花园了。有些客户觉得，如果他们周五就做出决定，周末就可以“好好想想”。对有些客户来说，决定继续推进你的项目会带来成就感，让他们从“待办事项”清单上划掉一项。

If the customer agrees to see you on a Friday afternoon, particularly if she is leaving on vacation, be assured she thinks you can solve her problem, or she has already decided to buy. This is a high-probability sales call. But don’t be overconfident. Be exceptionally prepared in order to close the order.

如果客户同意在周五下午与您见面，尤其是在她休假的情况下，请放心，她认为您能解决她的问题，或者她已经决定购买。这是一个高概率的销售拜访。但不要过度自信。为了达成订单，请做好充分的准备。

And the competition is not seeing customers on Friday afternoons. The other salespeople have started their weekend early. The other salespeople have left the arena, giving the Rainmaker an edge.

而且竞争对手周五下午不会接待客户。其他销售员都早早就开始了周末的行程。其他销售员都离开了赛场，这给了“雨人”一个优势。

“Break the Ice” at the End of the Sales Call

在销售电话结束时“打破僵局”

T here are all kinds of selling advice advocating the use of “icebreakers.” An icebreaker is supposed to be some clever observation or comment by the salesperson at the beginning of a sales call that “breaks the ice” between the customer and the salesperson. The salesperson is coached to look around the customer’s office to spot a piece of modern art or photos of kids playing soccer or a softball trophy and then to make an ice-breaking, bonding-type remark, “So, did you shoot that deer up there, or kill it with your car?”

各种各样的销售建议都提倡使用“破冰技巧”。破冰技巧指的是销售人员在销售拜访开始时巧妙的观察或评论，能够打破客户与销售人员之间的僵局。销售人员会被指导环顾客户的办公室，找到一件现代艺术品、孩子们踢足球的照片或一个垒球奖杯，然后说出一些有助于破冰、增进感情的话语：“那么，你刚才打死的那只鹿是打死的，还是用你的车撞死的？”

There is no ice between a Rainmaker and her customer. You have an appointment, a scheduled time. The customer knows the subject of the meeting. You are there to help the customer. Your help is far more important than his collection of rowing medals—and both of you know that! So get to the point of the meeting, as expected.

雨人与客户之间没有隔阂。你们有约定，有安排好的时间。客户知道会面的主题。你来是为了帮助客户。你的帮助远比他那些划船奖牌重要得多——你们双方都明白这一点！所以，正如预期的那样，直奔主题吧。

You will connect personally with your customer if you ask sincere, diagnostic-driven questions and if you listen carefully and thoughtfully to the answers. On a first sales call ask questions that encourage the customer to talk about her company, her goals, her expectations. Customers reward salespeople who listen.

如果你真诚地提出诊断性的问题，并认真仔细地倾听客户的回答，就能与客户建立起个人联系。第一次销售拜访时，要提出一些鼓励客户谈论公司、目标和期望的问题。客户会奖励那些认真倾听的销售人员。

Communication between Rainmaker and customer is of great importance. Problems are discussed. Financial investments are considered and made. All parties are concerned that the decisions are correct and that good outcomes ensue. Although positive, the experience has energy, highs, bits of doubt, and closure.

Rainmaker 与客户之间的沟通至关重要。沟通中会讨论问题，考虑并做出财务投资。各方都关心决策是否正确，以及能否带来良好的结果。虽然这种体验是积极的，但也充满能量、高潮、疑虑和最终的结局。

If you had two minutes to get the sale, you wouldn’t “break the ice” and comment on the suit of armor in the corner. So don’t make the comment if you have twenty minutes to make the sale. Once the customer has made a commitment, when he or she is walking you to the elevator, this is when conversation about children or baseball or the hassles of business travel can be healthy and relaxing.

如果你有两分钟的时间来促成交易，你就不会“打破僵局”，对角落里的盔甲评头论足。所以，如果你有二十分钟的时间来促成交易，也不要对它评头论足。一旦顾客做出承诺，在他或她送你去电梯的时候，谈论孩子、棒球或商务旅行的麻烦，才是健康轻松的时刻。

Icebreakers are for the Arctic Ocean, not for Rainmakers.

破冰船是为北冰洋服务的，不是为雨人服务的。

Use the Point System Every Day

每天使用积分系统

T here are four steps that are part of every sale.

每次销售都包含四个步骤。

They are:

它们是：

1.  Getting a lead, a referral, an introduction to a decision maker.

1. 获得线索、推荐、介绍给决策者。

2.  Getting an appointment to meet the decision maker.

2. 与决策者预约会面。

3.  Meeting the decision maker face-to-face.

3. 与决策者面对面会谈。

4. Getting a commitment to a close (a purchase) or to an action that directly leads to a close.

4. 获得完成交易（购买）的承诺或直接导致完成交易的行动。

Assign one point to Step 1, two points to Step 2, three points to Step 3, and four points to Step 4.

为步骤 1 分配一个点，为步骤 2 分配两个点，为步骤 3 分配三个点，为步骤 4 分配四个点。

Work every day to get a total of four points, in any combination of steps: four referrals, one referral and one face-to-face meeting, one commitment, and so on. You can shoot for more points per day if doable.

每天努力争取总共四分，具体步骤可以任意组合：四次推荐、一次推荐和一次面谈、一次承诺等等。如果可以的话，你可以争取每天获得更多积分。

At the top of your daily to do list put “Get 4 Points.” The key is to use the point system daily. Don’t wait until Friday and try to get twenty points.

在你的每日待办事项清单顶部写上“获得4分”。关键在于每天都要运用积分系统。不要等到周五才去争取20分。

If you tally four points per day, you will never run out of prospects, your pipeline will always be full, you will never have a slow period, and you will always be making rain.

如果你每天统计四个点，你将永远不会缺少潜在客户，你的销售管道将永远是满的，你将永远不会遇到销售淡季，而且你将永远创造奇迹。

Try this system diligently for fifteen business days, and then decide for yourself if it should become an integral part of your selling arsenal.

认真试用该系统十五个工作日，然后自行决定它是否应该成为您销售武器库中不可或缺的一部分。

A Shot on Goal Is Never a Bad Play

射门永远不是坏事

R ainmakers go for it. They never negatively prejudge a sales event. Rainmakers never say “We’re too small for that company,” or “We’ll never get an appointment with that guy.” Rainmakers answer the question “Why should that customer do business with us?” and then they go for it.

雨人勇于尝试。他们从不对销售活动做出负面预判。雨人从不说“我们对那家公司来说太小了”，或者“我们永远也预约不到那个人”。雨人会回答“为什么那个客户应该和我们做生意？”这个问题，然后勇于尝试。

Wayne Gretzky, the National Hockey League’s greatest all-time scorer, said, “One thousand percent of the shots I don’t take don’t go in.”

国家冰球联盟 (National Hockey League) 历史上最伟大的得分手韦恩·格雷茨基 (Wayne Gretzky) 曾说过：“我没有出手的投篮百分之一千都不会进。”

The Rainmaker knows one reality: If he doesn’t make the selling attempt, there will be no sale.

雨人知道一个现实：如果他不努力销售，就不会有销售。

A specialty metals salesperson had just finished a few days of unusual sales training. The training featured, to this salesperson’s mind, radical ideas. The salesperson was told that the lowest price was not the same thing as the lowest cost, and that the highest-priced product could, in fact, represent the lowest cost of ownership to a customer. The salesperson was told that if the customer simply agrees to an appointment, then the customer is predisposed to buying. The salesperson heard a number of other selling notions that he knew, based on thirty years of experience, might work elsewhere but were bogus for “his” industry.

一位特种金属销售员刚刚完成了几天不同寻常的销售培训。在这位销售员看来，培训内容充满了激进的理念。他被告知，最低价格并不等同于最低成本，事实上，最高价格的产品可能代表着客户最低的拥有成本。他还被告知，如果客户只是同意预约，那么客户就倾向于购买。根据他三十年的经验，他知道，这些销售理念在其他地方可能行得通，但在“他的”行业里却完全是骗人的。

To prove the irrelevance of the training, the salesperson called on a potential customer who had never purchased from his company and, he assumed, never would because of his company’s reputation for high prices, albeit good quality. To the salesperson’s surprise, the customer agreed to see him. After just one sales call the “never will buy” customer stunned the salesperson with a $25,000 order. The salesperson now has a new attitude.

为了证明培训的无关紧要，这位销售人员拜访了一位从未在公司购买过产品的潜在客户，并认为这位客户永远不会再购买，因为他的公司虽然质量好，但价格却很高。令销售人员惊讶的是，这位客户竟然同意了。仅仅一次销售拜访之后，这位“永远不会购买”的客户就以一笔2.5万美元的订单震惊了销售人员。这位销售人员现在态度焕然一新。

The 1980 U.S. Olympic hockey team—amateurs and college kids—had no chance against the mighty Russian squad—all professionals and veterans. And a last-second, ninety-foot shot was never going through the legs of the world’s best goalie. But it did. And the United States won.

1980年美国奥运冰球队——由业余选手和大学生组成——在强大的俄罗斯队面前毫无胜算——俄罗斯队全部由职业选手和老将组成。最后一秒，90英尺外的射门，根本无法穿过世界最佳守门员的双腿。但它却射中了。美国队最终获胜。

Rainmakers take shots on a goal.

雨人队射门。

Don’t Make Cold Calls

不要打电话

A cold call is when a salesperson visits a customer without an appointment. A cold call is a remnant of the days of door-to-door salespeople, when seeing as many people as possible was one way to succeed. Today, cold-calling is generally used by telemarketing people to prospect for customers.

冷呼叫是指销售人员未经预约直接上门拜访客户。冷呼叫是上门推销时代的遗留，当时，拜访尽可能多的人是成功的秘诀之一。如今，电话营销人员通常使用冷呼叫来寻找客户。

Cold calls don’t work. No busy decision maker has the time to drop what she is doing to see someone she doesn’t know.

主动联系根本行不通。没有哪个忙碌的决策者有时间放下手头的工作去拜访一个不认识的人。

Cold calls are an intrusion and, to some, a sign of poor manners. A cold call is a gamble: You don’t know if the customer is qualified, has a problem, or even if he or she is there.

打陌生电话是一种侵犯，对某些人来说，甚至是一种不礼貌的表现。打陌生电话就像一场赌博：你不知道客户是否合格，是否有问题，甚至不知道他/她是否在场。

Cold calls indicate poor planning. They indicate that the salesperson is not doing a good job qualifying leads or getting appointments. The old selling adage is instructive: Plan your work, and work your plan.

冷拨电话表明计划不周。这表明销售人员在筛选潜在客户或促成预约方面做得不好。有句古老的销售格言很有启发：规划你的工作，然后按照计划执行。

Instead of cold calls use the point system.

不要使用陌生电话，而要使用积分系统。

But what happens if, due to a legitimate emergency, a scheduled appointment is canceled at the last minute? It is Friday afternoon; you try not to be discouraged. You roll your eyes heavenward and spot a light burning in an office in a factory across the way. Maybe they are a prospect, you muse. What the heck, you think as you walk into the lobby, a shot on goal is never a bad play.

但如果真的有紧急情况，预约在最后一刻被取消了怎么办？现在是星期五下午，你努力不让自己灰心丧气。你翻了个白眼，发现对面一家工厂的办公室里亮着灯。你心想，也许他们是个潜在客户。管他呢，你一边走进大厅，一边想，射门总归是不错的选择。

Show the Chain, Sell the First Link

展示链条，销售第一个环节

N o one buys a chain link by link. No one goes into a hardware store and says, “Give me seventeen links,” or “Let me have a box of links.” People either buy the whole chain or they don’t. It is the same with a sale. If the customer is shown all the steps in a sale and agrees to the first step, the customer has bought the chain… unless you break it.

没有人会一环一环地买链条。没有人会走进五金店说：“给我十七个链环”或“给我一盒链环”。人们要么买整条链条，要么不买。销售也是如此。如果顾客了解了销售的所有步骤，并且同意第一步，那么他们就购买了整条链条……除非你把它弄坏了。

Showing the customer the step-by-step, agreement-by-agreement process, from first sales call to purchase order, is a compelling selling technique. Only Rainmakers use this technique. Most salespeople either don’t know all the steps, or don’t understand the linkage, or don’t plan strategically, or are afraid of showing their hand.

向客户展示从首次销售电话到最终达成采购订单的逐步、逐一的流程，是一种令人信服的销售技巧。只有“雨人”才会使用这种技巧。大多数销售人员要么不了解所有步骤，要么不理解其中的关联，要么没有进行战略规划，要么害怕展现自己的实力。

A super salesperson for a specialty chemical manufacturer is a champ at showing the chain and selling the first link, thereby selling the chain and closing the order. At her first meeting with a prospective customer she proceeds as follows: “Mr. Customer, we have a great deal of success in this type of application, always giving you, the customer, a positive dollarized return on your investment.

一家特种化学品制造商的超级销售员非常擅长展示整个销售链，并在第一环节就销售出去，最终促成整个销售链的销售并最终达成订单。在与潜在客户的第一次会面中，她会这样说道：“客户先生，我们在这类应用方面取得了巨大的成功，我们总能为您，也就是客户，带来实实在在的投资回报。”

“Assuming we can give you such a return, would you like to know the typical steps involved in solving this problem?

“假设我们可以给你这样的回报，你想知道解决这个问题的典型步骤吗？

“OK, good. First, we do a plant tour, and look at exactly how you assemble the product. Second, we get production samples of your product. We break them down and reengineer them, looking for ways to reduce assembly costs. Next, we work with you to develop an investment return analysis. Together we calculate how much money the recommended solution will save your company—or conversely, how much money it will cost you to go without this solution. Of course, you have to agree to the total amount of money you will be saving your company, OK?

好的，很好。首先，我们会参观工厂，详细了解您产品的组装方式。其次，我们会获取您产品的生产样品。我们会对其进行分解和重新设计，寻找降低组装成本的方法。接下来，我们会与您一起进行投资回报分析。我们会共同计算推荐的解决方案能为您的公司节省多少钱——或者反过来说，如果不采用该解决方案，您将损失多少钱。当然，您必须同意您能为公司节省的总金额，好吗？

“Good. Next, we do a test of our product here in your factory. If the test is successful, we go to a limited production run. All right?

很好。接下来，我们会在你们工厂测试我们的产品。如果测试成功，我们就会进行小批量生产。好吗？

“Good. If the test is successful, and the limited production run meets your criteria, we decide on a delivery date for your first full run production quantity. That’s about it. Any questions?

很好。如果测试成功，并且限量生产符合您的标准，我们将确定首批全量生产的交货日期。就这样。还有问题吗？

“OK, great. That outlines the approach. Let’s take that plant tour, OK?”

“好的，太好了。这概述了方法。我们去参观一下工厂，好吗？”

When the customer agrees to “take that plant tour” the customer has agreed to buy the first link… and, in effect, buys the whole chain.

当客户同意“参观工厂”时，客户就同意购买第一个环节……实际上是购买整个链条。

The Rainmaker shows the chain, makes it clear how the phases in the sale are linked—from first agreement to purchase order—and then sells the first link. The first link is attached to the last link.

Rainmaker 展现了销售链条，清晰地展现了销售过程中各个阶段是如何联系在一起的——从最初的协议到最终的订单——然后销售了第一个环节。第一个环节与最后一个环节紧密相连。

Sell the first link and you sell the chain.

卖出第一个环节，你就卖出了整条链条。

嘴里有食物时不要说话

Bad table manners are off-putting; they signal insensitivity to others, an overly self-interested person, and an incomplete education.

不良的餐桌礼仪令人不快；这表明一个人对别人漠不关心、过于自私，而且教育不完整。

Drop your membership in the clean-the-plate club.

退出“光盘行动”俱乐部。

To Rainmakers, manners matter.

对于 Rainmakers 来说，礼仪很重要。

Killer Sales Question #5

杀手级销售问题 #5

R ight now, this second, take a quick break from reading. Try to close this book. Close this book, put it down, then reopen and start reading. (Note: You are here .)

现在，就在这一秒，暂时放下阅读。试着合上这本书。合上它，放下，然后重新打开，开始阅读。（注：你在这里。）

You either closed the book or you didn’t. Ask someone to toss you a coin, or a pencil, or anything. They either toss it or they don’t. You can’t “try” to do something; you either do it or you don’t.

你要么合上书，要么不合上。请别人向你抛硬币、铅笔或任何东西。他们要么抛，要么不抛。你不能“尝试”去做某事；你要么做，要么不做。

To close the sale, to get the final customer commitment, the Rainmaker might say: “You’ve looked at everything. Your concerns have been answered. Time is of the essence. You’ve heard our recommendation. Why don’t you give it a try?”

为了达成交易，获得最终的客户承诺，雨人可能会说：“您已经查看了所有内容。您的顾虑已经得到解答。时间至关重要。您已经听取了我们的建议。为什么不尝试一下呢？”

“Why don’t you give it a try?” is a killer sales question.

“你为什么不尝试一下呢？”这是一个极具吸引力的销售问题。

The “it” is your product.

这个“它”就是您的产品。

“Why don’t you give it a try?” is not the same as “Why don’t you try it?” or “Try it for a few days.” To try a product for a few days is a trial. Getting a trial is a good selling strategy, but it is an interim step, not the final step, to getting a sale.

“你为什么不试试看？”和“你为什么不试试这个？”或“试用几天？”不一样。试用产品几天是一种试用。获得试用是一个好的销售策略，但它是促成销售的过渡步骤，而非最终步骤。

To give something “a try” is, to most people, a revocable act, a decision that can be reversed. It feels temporary, impermanent. Subconsciously, people feel that to try something is to sample, to test, not a commitment to a decision. There is an assumed escape clause built into an agreement to give something a try.

对大多数人来说，“尝试”是一种可撤销的行为，一个可以逆转的决定。它给人的感觉是暂时的、无常的。潜意识里，人们觉得尝试只是个小尝试，测试一下，而不是对某个决定的承诺。在同意尝试某件事的协议中，通常包含一个假定的免责条款。

But people don’t try: They act, they do something.

但人们不会尝试：他们会行动，他们会做某事。

A super saleswoman sold a $1-million computer conversion that took eighteen months to implement by asking the customer, “Well, why don’t you give it a try?”

一位超级女销售员在销售价值 100 万美元、耗时 18 个月才完成的计算机改装产品时，问了顾客一句“好吧，你为什么不试一试呢？”

Love Voice Mail

爱情语音邮件

H ave you ever thought: If I could just get the guy alone, I could sell him. If so, voice mail is one answer. Voice mail is a good selling tool.

你有没有想过：如果我能单独和他联系，我就能把他卖掉。如果是这样，语音信箱就是一个答案。语音信箱是一个很好的销售工具。

Voice mail can be a selling opportunity for the Rainmaker. Voice mail gives the salesperson an uninterrupted period of time to communicate a meaningful dollarized benefit to the decision maker.

语音邮件可以成为“雨人”的销售机会。语音邮件让销售人员有一段不受干扰的时间，可以向决策者传达有意义的收益。

The objective of your voice-mail message is to get the customer to call you back, or for the customer to take your next call or to want to meet you. The key to voice-mail selling is to leave a compelling message, something that resonates positively with your customer.

语音邮件的目标是让客户回电，或者接听您的下一个电话，或者希望与您见面。语音邮件销售的关键在于留下引人入胜的信息，让客户产生积极的共鸣。

To be able to leave a good message the salesperson must accurately answer the question “Why should this customer do business with me?” You must answer the questions “Why should the customer call me back?” and “Why should the customer listen to me the next time I call?”

为了能够留下良好的信息，销售人员必须准确回答这个问题“为什么这个客户应该和我做生意？”你必须回答这些问题“为什么客户应该给我回电话？”和“为什么客户应该在我下次打电话时听我说？”

The answers to these questions must represent a significant benefit to the customer.

这些问题的答案必须能给客户带来显著的利益。

Here are voice-mail-usage guidelines:

以下是语音邮件使用指南：

• To answer the question “Why should the customer listen?” requires homework and analysis. To give the customer even an estimated sense of the dollarized value you represent necessitates precall planning.

• 要回答“客户为什么要听？”这个问题，需要做好充分的准备和分析。为了让客户对你所代表的金钱价值有一个大致的了解，就需要提前做好拜访前的规划。

• Brainstorm messages.

• 集思广益。

• Prepare your voice-mail message in writing. The core of this message should be a summary of the ultimate value you will bring the customer, and something you will use on a phone call, in a written letter, and in a face-to-face meeting. Preplan the message carefully. Keep it short; no more than thirty seconds .

• 准备书面语音邮件。语音邮件的核心内容应概括您将为客户带来的最终价值，以及您将在电话沟通、书面信函和面对面会议中运用的内容。请仔细规划语音邮件内容。保持简短，不超过三十秒。

• Consider using a third-party reference to set up your call and give you borrowed credibility. For example, “Dr. Jones in radiology at Saint Francis Hospital recommended that I introduce myself to you.”

• 考虑通过第三方推荐来安排通话，并借此提升你的信誉。例如，“圣弗朗西斯医院放射科的琼斯医生推荐我向你介绍自己。”

• Practice your voice-mail message.

• 练习您的语音邮件留言。

• Be ready to convey your message if the customer picks up the phone.

• 如果客户拿起电话，准备好传达您的信息。

• Speak slowly, clearly, and distinctly.

• 说话要慢、清楚、明确。

• Introduce yourself first. Be sure your name is easily understood. If you have a reference, state that person’s name clearly.

• 首先介绍自己。确保你的名字容易被理解。如果有推荐人，请清楚地写出推荐人的名字。

• State how long your voice message will be.

• 说明您的语音留言的长度。

• State the purpose of your call—to alert the customer to a dollarized opportunity now available.

• 说明您致电的目的——提醒客户现在有一个赚钱的机会。

• State the benefit and dollarized value.

• 说明收益和美元价值。

• Suggest a limited time frame for your ultimate meeting.

• 建议为最终会议设定一个有限的时间范围。

• Give your telephone number, and speak slowly. Do not rush your telephone number. Always say “area code” before reciting your three-digit area code. When giving the seven-digit number pause between numbers. Then repeat the phone number.

• 提供您的电话号码，并放慢语速。不要急于说出您的电话号码。在念出您的三位数区号之前，务必先说“区号”。提供七位数号码时，请在数字之间停顿。然后重复电话号码。

• Thank the customer and tell her that if she doesn’t get a chance to return your call, you will follow up.

• 感谢客户并告诉她，如果她没有机会回电，你会跟进。

To illustrate:

举例来说：

Good afternoon, Mr. Smith. A mutual friend, Jim Murphy, suggested I contact you. This message will take less than thirty seconds of your time. My name is Jeffrey Fox. The purpose of this call is to let you know of an opportunity that seems just perfect for you and your company. Based on analysis, you can reduce the manufacturing cost of the golf carts you sell by 12 percent, or approximately $900,000 a year. To see how you would save $900,000 a year will take about fifteen minutes. My number is area code 2-1-1, 9-8-7, 7-zero-zero-zero. Let me repeat that number: area code 2-1-1-, 9-8-7, 7-zero-zero-zero. If you can’t reach me, I will follow up. Thank you very much.

下午好，史密斯先生。我们共同的朋友吉姆·墨菲建议我联系您。这条消息只需不到三十秒的时间。我叫杰弗里·福克斯。这次打电话的目的是让您知道一个对您和您的公司来说似乎绝佳的机会。根据分析，您可以将所售高尔夫球车的制造成本降低12%，即每年约90万美元。要了解如何每年节省90万美元，大约需要十五分钟。我的电话号码是区号2-1-1，9-8-7，7-0-0-0。让我重复一遍：区号2-1-1-，9-8-7，7-0-0-0。如果您联系不上我，我会跟进。非常感谢。

When next you speak with your target customer, be prepared to say “Do you have your appointment calendar handy?”

下次与目标客户交谈时，准备好问“您手边有预约日历吗？”

Park in the Back

停在后面

C ustomers begin assessing salespeople in seconds. It is natural for some customers to build mental moats to protect themselves from making a decision to invest money in your product. They begin building mental defense systems and making the assessment as soon as they see you. So you want the customer to see you when you are organized and ready.

顾客会在几秒钟内开始评估销售人员。有些顾客会自然而然地建立心理护城河，保护自己不去决定是否投资你的产品。他们一见到你，就会开始建立心理防御系统，并做出评估。所以，你希望顾客在你准备就绪、准备就绪时看到你。

You don’t want the customer to see you crabbing out of a car, struggling into a jacket, straightening your skirt, taming your hair, fumbling with your briefcase. You don’t want the customer to see you as anything but prompt and professional. You don’t want the customer seeing you as vulnerable.

你不想让顾客看到你从车里走出来，费力地套上外套，整理裙子，整理头发，笨手笨脚地摆弄公文包。你不想让顾客觉得你不够迅速和专业。你不想让顾客觉得你很脆弱。

Never show vulnerability. Always be confident. Plan for the unexpected. Expect a curve ball. Stay calm. Remember the old poker-playing axiom: Never let them see you sweat. Never reveal a weakness, such as not feeling well. Customers don’t care about your illness. If a customer asks how you are feeling, simply answer “Splendidly, thank you.”

切勿展现脆弱。始终保持自信。未雨绸缪，准备应对意外情况。预料到情况会突然变化。保持冷静。记住那条古老的扑克牌规则：永远不要让别人看到你汗流浃背。切勿暴露弱点，例如身体不适。顾客不会在意你的病情。如果顾客询问你感觉如何，只需回答“非常好，谢谢”。

Park in the back. Get ready.

把车停在后面。做好准备。

Rainmakers show up fit and ready.

雨人已做好准备。

Be the Best-Dressed Person You Will Meet Today

成为今天见到的穿着最得体的人

F riday is dress-down day,” but not for the Rainmaker. The Rainmaker does not dress down, nor does he necessarily dress up. He dresses better than any customer he will meet that day. If the customer wears polo shirts and sneakers, the Rainmaker wears a blazer and loafers. If the customer wears slacks and a blouse, the Rainmaker wears a pants suit. If the customer wears polyester, the Rainmaker wears wool. Warning: You are not trying to one-up your client; you are letting the customer know he or she is important to you.

“星期五是便装日”，但 Rainmaker 却不然。Rainmaker 不会穿得随意，也不一定盛装打扮。他比当天遇到的任何顾客都穿得好。如果顾客穿 Polo 衫和运动鞋，Rainmaker 就会穿西装外套和休闲鞋。如果顾客穿休闲裤和衬衫，Rainmaker 就会穿裤装。如果顾客穿涤纶衣服，Rainmaker 就会穿羊毛衣服。警告：你不是想胜过你的客户；你是想让客户知道他或她对你很重要。

Don’t succumb to the lure of “business casual.” When you are trying to attract new business, nothing is casual. Your customer wants you to be “buttoned up” and professional.

不要被“商务休闲”的诱惑所吸引。当你试图吸引新客户时，没有什么是休闲的。你的客户希望你穿着得体、专业。

But don’t overdress. Don’t overwhelm the customer with flamboyant sartorial splendor. Your dress should signal confidence, success, expertise, sensitivity, professionalism, and attention to detail.

但不要穿得太夸张。不要用华丽的服饰来压倒顾客。你的着装应该展现你的自信、成功、专业、敏锐、敬业以及对细节的关注。

Dressing with care flatters your customer. It is said that President Ronald Reagan had such respect for the Oval Office that he never entered unless dressed in suit and tie. The American people respected Mr. Reagan’s respect, and perhaps it was one reason they reelected him in a landslide. Your respect for your customer will show, and your customer will appreciate it; your customer will reelect you, sale after sale.

精心的着装能让你的客户感到宾至如归。据说罗纳德·里根总统对椭圆形办公室非常尊重，除非穿着西装打着领带，否则他绝不会进入。美国人民敬重里根先生，这或许也是他们以压倒性优势再次选举他的原因之一。你对客户的尊重会体现出来，你的客户也会感激你的付出；你的客户会通过一次又一次的销售再次选择你。

Why Breakfast Meetings Bring Rain

为什么早餐会会带来麻烦

B reakfast is an excellent time to do business with a prospective customer. A hugely successful Rainmaker, the late multibusiness owner Clayton Gengras of Connecticut, once remarked, “All the money I’ve made that stuck to my fingers, I made before eight o’clock in the morning.” Breakfast jump-starts the day. Here’s why:

早餐是与潜在客户洽谈生意的绝佳时机。康涅狄格州已故的多元化企业主克莱顿·根格拉斯是一位非常成功的“雨人”，他曾说过：“我赚到的所有钱，都是在早上八点之前赚到的。” 早餐是开启一天的绝佳时机。原因如下：

• The customer knows the purpose of a breakfast meeting is not to discuss the World Series or to rate one cereal over another. When you arranged the meeting you gave the customer an idea of the purpose (which is some commitment by the customer to an action that leads to a sale). Consequently, when a customer agrees to meet you for breakfast, he or she is making an uncommon investment of time. That investment is a positive buy signal.

• 客户知道早餐会的目的并非讨论世界职业棒球大赛，也不是评价某种谷物食品好坏。您在安排早餐会时，就已向客户明确了其目的（即客户承诺采取某种行动，最终促成销售）。因此，当客户同意与您共进早餐时，他/她正在做出一项非同寻常的时间投入。这项投入是一个积极的购买信号。

• Breakfast is usually less expensive than a business lunch or dinner. The menu is simple, requiring less time to make a selection, which means more time for discussion. You don’t have to be concerned about alcoholic beverages.

• 早餐通常比商务午餐或晚餐便宜。菜单简单，选择时间更短，这意味着有更多的时间讨论。您不必担心酒精饮料。

• Breakfast saves your customer time. Choose a venue that is on the customer’s route to work; this eliminates one of the “from office, back to office” trips associated with other outside meetings.

• 早餐可以节省客户的时间。选择位于客户上班路线上的地点，这样可以避免像其他外出会议那样“往返办公室”的麻烦。

• Breakfast meetings are less vulnerable to cancellations. They happen before the customer’s daily problems begin. And the customer is fresh, alert, and eager.

• 早餐会不太可能被取消。早餐会安排在客户日常问题出现之前。而且客户此时精神饱满、警觉性高、热情高涨。

The choice of restaurant is less important for breakfast. It is hard to serve lousy tea and toast. Convenience to the customer is the important selection criteria. Don’t go to a popular take-out place with a zillion people going in and out. Don’t go to the local diner if it’s a hangout for a motorcycle club. Don’t go to the so-called power breakfast joints. They can be distracting. Those places are to show off; they are for show biz, not to do biz.

选择哪家餐厅吃早餐其实没那么重要。糟糕的茶和吐司很难让人接受。方便顾客才是重要的选择标准。不要去人来人往、人气爆棚的外卖店。如果当地小餐馆是摩托车俱乐部的聚集地，也不要去。不要去那些所谓的“权力早餐店”。它们会让人分心。那些地方是用来炫耀的；它们是用来表演的，不是用来做生意的。

After you have received your customer’s commitment and the meeting has concluded, don’t walk out of the restaurant with your customer. Let your customer leave in peace and privacy. Excuse yourself to make a phone call.

收到顾客的承诺并结束会面后，请勿陪同顾客离开餐厅。请让顾客安静地离开，并留下您打电话的借口。

One Rainmaker regularly schedules two breakfasts in a single morning. He jump-starts the day with two sales calls before most people even get to work.

有一位“雨人”经常在一个早晨安排两顿早餐。在大多数人上班之前，他就会打两通销售电话，开启新的一天。

“Here’s My Card…”

“这是我的名片……”

D on’t forget to use your business card. To too many people the business card is so common, so trivial, that they forget its purpose. Business cards are to get and keep customers, to get into a customer’s address book, not to go into a bowl to win a free lunch.

别忘了用你的名片。对很多人来说，名片太普通、太琐碎了，以至于他们忘记了它的用途。名片是为了吸引和留住客户，是为了记录在客户的通讯录里，而不是为了捞取免费的午餐。

Business cards should not be cute, cluttered, or clunky. Olde English script with curves and curliques is not classy; it is hard to read. Don’t put every product you make and every logo in your organization on your card. Less is more.

名片不应该太过花哨、凌乱或笨重。带有曲线和花饰的古英语字体既不雅观，也难以阅读。不要把你生产的所有产品和公司的所有标志都印在名片上。少即是多。

A noted criminal attorney, a fantastic Rainmaker, consistently gave his card to bartenders, cabdrivers, waiters, construction workers—anyone. “Here’s my card; if you ever need help, or anyone you know needs help, give me a call. We’ll help you.”

一位著名的刑事律师，一位出色的“雨人”，总是把自己的名片递给调酒师、出租车司机、服务员、建筑工人——任何人。“这是我的名片；如果你需要帮助，或者你认识的任何人需要帮助，就给我打电话。我们会帮你的。”

One real estate agent, for fifteen years the number one agent in her market, is always courteous but never bashful. “Here’s my card. If you ever consider buying or selling real estate, give me a call. You will get special treatment.”

一位房地产经纪人，十五年来一直是她所在市场的领军人物，她总是彬彬有礼，却从不害羞。“这是我的名片。如果您考虑买卖房产，请给我打电话。您会得到特殊待遇。”

A partner in an international accounting firm became partner in part because target clients got his card. “Here’s my card. If you or your company want to reduce taxes and optimize cash flow, give me a call. You will get our best people.”

一家国际会计师事务所的合伙人之所以能成为合伙人，部分原因就是他的目标客户拿到了他的名片。“这是我的名片。如果您或您的公司想减税并优化现金流，就给我打电话。我们会为您提供最优秀的人才。”

The owner of an upscale antique gallery didn’t wait for customers to come to him. He often met business owners, and when he did, he handed them his business card. They were engraved, rich in tone. “Here is my card. Your elegant boardroom is a wonderful place for our elegant antiques. We would be flattered if you would ask us for a recommendation.”

一家高档古董画廊的老板从不等待顾客上门。他经常会见一些企业主，见到他们时，他会递上自己的名片。名片上雕刻着精美的图案，色调浓郁。“这是我的名片。您那间雅致的会议室是我们收藏精美古董的绝佳场所。如果您能请我们推荐，我们将不胜荣幸。”

Rainmakers know why business cards are called business cards.

Rainmakers 知道名片为何被称为名片。

Killer Sales Question #6

杀手销售问题 #6

A complete understanding of the customer’s needs, wants, concerns, objections, options, budget, and timetable is crucial to the Rainmaker. The Rainmaker must learn all that is relevant from the customer. The learning list is exhaustive and includes knowing the concerns of the customer’s colleagues, determining the competitors, and gaining an intimate understanding of the problem.

对“雨人”来说，全面了解客户的需求、愿望、顾虑、反对意见、选择、预算和时间表至关重要。“雨人”必须从客户那里了解所有相关信息。学习内容详尽无遗，包括了解客户同事的顾虑、确定竞争对手，以及深入了解问题所在。

The Rainmaker prepares for the input sessions with carefully crafted needs analyses and situation-understanding questions. No question is too trivial, too obvious, too mundane to ask. The goal is to diagnose the problem and to discover how your product or service will be of benefit to the customer.

Rainmaker 会精心准备需求分析和情况理解问题，为客户意见征集环节做好准备。任何问题，无论多么琐碎、多么明显、多么平凡，都值得一问。目标是诊断问题，并发现您的产品或服务将如何惠及客户。

Regardless of the quality of the questions, and regardless of the willingness of the customer to provide information, the Rainmaker always assumes he missed something. The Rainmaker always concludes an interview with a customer by asking one killer sales question.

无论问题质量如何，也无论客户是否愿意提供信息，雨人总是认为自己漏掉了什么。雨人总是在与客户面谈结束时，提出一个绝妙的销售问题。

The killer sales question is: “What question should I be asking that I am not asking?” Variants, or follow-up questions, are: “Is there anything I have missed?” “Have I covered everything?” “Have I asked about every detail that is important to you?”

杀手级销售问题是：“我应该问什么问题而我却没有问？” 变体或后续问题是：“我遗漏了什么吗？” “我是否涵盖了所有内容？” “我是否询问了对您来说重要的每个细节？”

If you have covered everything, you’re OK. If not, the killer sales question will unearth something that’s important to the customer. The Rainmaker dissects the answer with probing follow-up questions.

如果你已经涵盖了所有内容，那就没问题了。如果没有，那么关键的销售问题会揭示出对客户来说很重要的东西。“雨人”会用深入的后续问题来剖析答案。

“What am I not asking?” is asked by the most confident, most customer-concerned, most professional of professionals. And good customers want to be asked this fantastic leave-no-stone-unturned question.

“我还有啥没问？”最自信、最关心客户、最专业的专业人士都会问这个问题。优秀的客户希望被问到这个绝妙的、无所不包的问题。

Rainmakers ask the questions others wish they had asked.

祈雨者会问出其他人希望问的问题。

How to Recognize a Rainmaker

如何识别雨人

W hat is the single attribute that characterizes the Rainmaker—the best salesperson? What distinguishes the markedly great salesperson from the merely good? Now, stop reading, close your eyes, and consider for a moment what is the single outstanding characteristic of a great salesperson.…

造雨人——最优秀的销售员——的特质是什么？一位极其优秀的销售员和一位仅仅优秀的销售员之间有什么区别？现在，请停止阅读，闭上眼睛，思考一下一位优秀销售员的突出特质是什么。

There are many “good” salespeople; there are far fewer “great” salespeople. The good salesperson has a variety of success-creating habits and attributes. The good salesperson:

“优秀”的销售人员很多，但“卓越”的销售人员却少之又少。优秀的销售人员拥有各种有助于取得成功的习惯和特质。优秀的销售人员：

• is organized

• 有组织

• calls only on decision makers

• 仅呼吁决策者

• does detailed precall planning

• 进行详细的拜访前规划

• always has a written sales call objective

• 始终有书面的销售拜访目标

• asks preplanned questions

• 提出预先计划好的问题

• listens

• 倾听

• is empathetic with customers

• 对客户富有同理心

• encourages and appreciates objections

• 鼓励并赞赏反对意见

• always dollarizes the value of the product

• 始终将产品价值美元化

• asks for customer commitments

• 要求客户做出承诺

and a hundred other things, from being properly dressed, to composing excellent communications, to faultless follow up.

以及其他上百件事，从穿着得体，到撰写出色的通信，再到完美的后续行动。

Those talents are all important.

这些才能都很重要。

But the one thing that separates the number one salesperson from all the rest is that the number one salesperson sells more .

但是，第一名销售员与其他销售员之间的区别在于，第一名销售员的销量更高。

When the score is tallied, it doesn’t matter how hard someone worked, or how many brilliant memos someone wrote, or how perfect the monthly reports. It doesn’t matter how clever the conversation, how hip the clothes, how smooth the style. The only score that counts is how much money has been generated.

在计分时，一个人工作多么努力，写了多少精彩的备忘录，或者月度报告多么完美，都无关紧要。他的谈吐多么机灵，他的衣着多么时尚，他的作风多么流畅，都无关紧要。唯一重要的分数是创造了多少钱。

If you have a Rainmaker, or Rainmakers, in your organization, you are fortunate. It matters not if your Rainmaker is a prima donna, an independent loner, or difficult to “manage.” It matters not if your Rainmaker doesn’t play by your rules, is indifferent to your policies, or is always late with expense accounts.

如果你的组织里有一位或多位“雨人”，那你真是幸运。无论你的“雨人”是自命不凡、独来独往还是难以“管理”，都无关紧要。无论你的“雨人”不遵守你的规则、对你的政策漠不关心，还是总是拖欠报销款，都无关紧要。

What matters is the Rainmaker’s ability to ring the cash register, to put money in the till, to bring in new clients. As long as the Rainmaker obeys the laws of God and man, and stays within budget, you must let him make rain.

重要的是“雨人”的能力，它能敲响收银机，把钱放进收银机，带来新客户。只要“雨人”遵守神与人的法则，并且不超出预算，你就必须让他造雨。

Tolerate your Rainmaker. Teach your Rainmaker. Train your Rainmaker.

容忍你的 Rainmaker。教导你的 Rainmaker。训练你的 Rainmaker。

Rainmakers bring the customers who bring the money that makes the organization flourish.

造雨人带来客户，而客户又带来金钱，从而使组织繁荣发展。

A RAINMAKER EXTRA: HOW TO DOLLARIZE

雨人额外福利：如何美元化

Y ou are in the paint store evaluating two brands of house paint. Brand A is $10 a gallon, and Brand B is $18 a gallon. Brand A has the lowest price, but Brand B has more pigment, thereby requiring one less coat of paint than Brand A. Which paint has the lowest cost?

你在一家油漆店里，正在评估两种品牌的家用油漆。A品牌每加仑10美元，B品牌每加仑18美元。A品牌价格最低，但B品牌颜料含量更高，因此比A品牌少涂一层油漆。哪种油漆成本最低？

To compare the true costs of each product, you must determine the total costs associated with each product. The process of making this evaluation is dollarization. Dollarization is figuring out—in dollars and cents—what each product is really worth to the customer.

要比较每种产品的真实成本，必须确定每种产品相关的总成本。进行此评估的过程称为“美元化”。“美元化”指的是以美元和美分计算出每种产品对消费者的实际价值。

In the house paint example, the customer or the salesperson or both calculate that ten gallons of Brand A is needed—a $100 job. Brand B can do the job with five gallons, or for $90. The labor cost for Brand A is twice that for Brand B. Brand B is the lowest net cost solution.

以房屋油漆为例，客户或销售人员（或两者）计算出需要10加仑A品牌油漆，即100美元。B品牌油漆只需5加仑即可完成，价格为90美元。A品牌的人工成本是B品牌的两倍。B品牌是净成本最低的解决方案。

Price is the universal measure customers use to compare two products. However, if the customer’s true goal is to get the lowest total cost, then focusing only on price is myopic.

价格是消费者比较两种产品的通用标准。然而，如果消费者真正的目标是获得最低的总成本，那么只关注价格就显得目光短浅了。

Almost all sellers claim benefits for their products such as “faster,” “stronger,” “longer lasting,” “superior quality,” “more durable,” “more efficient.” Occasionally, the customer intuitively dollarizes the value of these claims and correctly selects the product that yields the lowest total cost. But more often, the seller, despite having the best solution, is reduced to fighting a price battle, because the seller does not know what “faster” means, or does not know how to translate “faster” into dollars and cents.

几乎所有卖家都会宣传其产品具有“更快”、“更强”、“更持久”、“更优质”、“更耐用”、“更高效”等优点。有时，顾客会本能地将这些宣传的价值转化为金钱，并正确地选择总成本最低的产品。但更多时候，即使卖家拥有最佳解决方案，也只能陷入价格战，因为他们不知道“更快”的含义，或者不知道如何将“更快”转化为金钱。

Sellers frequently have a difficult time placing a precise value on the benefits they provide.

卖家经常很难准确评估他们所提供的利益的价值。

For example, you are a salesperson for a gasket company. Your target customer buys gaskets to seal an engine component, and pays $.92 for each gasket. Your gasket is priced at $1.00. Because of a different design, your gasket is “more reliable”: It fails eight times less often per thousand gaskets than the competition. Each failure results in a warranty claim that costs $25.00 to fix. What is the true price of your gasket? Can you dollarize the true cost of your gasket?

例如，您是一家垫片公司的销售人员。您的目标客户购买垫片来密封发动机部件，每个垫片的价格为0.92美元。您的垫片售价为1美元。由于设计独特，您的垫片“更可靠”：每千个垫片的故障率比竞争对手低八倍。每次故障都会导致保修索赔，维修费用为25美元。您的垫片的真实价格是多少？您能用美元来计算垫片的真实成本吗？

Here is how the Rainmaker dollarizes the value of the gasket, and every other product, using six basic steps:

Rainmaker 使用以下六个基本步骤来将垫圈和其他所有产品的价值美元化：

1.  Determine the Competition

1. 确定竞争对手

State the other options your customer will be considering. Options could include an existing methodology, a competitor, or an in-house customer approach.

说明客户正在考虑的其他方案。这些方案可以包括现有方法、竞争对手或客户内部方案。

Example: The competitor is a proven supplier that sells its gasket for $.92.

示例：竞争对手是一家可靠的供应商，其垫圈的售价为 0.92 美元。

2.  State Your Benefit

2. 说明你的利益

State why your customer should do business with you.

说明为什么您的客户应该与您做生意。

Example: Our gaskets are more reliable.

例如：我们的垫圈更可靠。

3.  Quantify the Benefit

3.量化效益

Restate the benefit in numerical terms.

用数字形式重申其好处。

Example: “More reliable” gaskets means our customer faces eight fewer warranty claims per thousand products sold.

例如：“更可靠”的垫圈意味着我们的客户每售出一千件产品就会减少八次保修索赔。

4.  Dollarize the Benefit

4. 福利美元化

Calculate the dollar value of the benefit.

计算收益的美元价值。

Example:

例子：

5.  Express the Total Dollarized Benefit in “Per Unit” Terms

5. 以“每单位”形式表达总美元收益

Calculate the portion of the total economic benefit the customer realizes from each unit he purchases.

计算客户从其购买的每个单位中获得的总经济效益的份额。

Example:

例子：

6.  Demonstrate the True Net Cost of Your Product

6. 展示产品的真实净成本

Show how the total economic benefit derived from each product reveals the true net cost (or true price) of your product.

展示每种产品产生的总经济效益如何揭示产品的真实净成本（或真实价格）。

Example:

例子：

Because of the total savings your product provides, the true net price per unit of your product is only $.80. In effect, when the customer gives you $1.00 for each gasket, you give back to the customer $.20 in warranty cost savings. Eighty cents is the number the customer should use when comparing competitors’ prices.

由于您的产品能够带来总成本节省，您的产品每单位实际净价仅为 0.80 美元。实际上，当客户为每个垫圈支付 1.00 美元时，您就返还了客户 0.20 美元的保修成本节省。客户在与竞争对手比较价格时，应该使用 0.80 美元这个价格。

Dollarization is the Rainmaker’s edge. It is more effective to do the math and say “This air conditioner saves $14 a month in reduced electricity bills” than to simply say “This air conditioner is energy-efficient.”

美元化是 Rainmaker 的优势。算一下，说“这台空调每月节省 14 美元电费”，比简单地说“这台空调很节能”更有效。

Three of the most important words in the Rainmaker’s dictionary are dollarize, dollarize, dollarize!

Rainmaker 词典中最重要的三个词是美元化、美元化、美元化！

A CASE STUDY: MR. K.

案例研究：K 先生

A rguably the best salesman in the U.S. wine industry recently concluded an outstanding career as the chairman of one of the country’s finest premium wine companies. For over thirty years, he personally sold millions of dollars’ worth of wine, and many of those sales were made well before wine was as fashionable as it is today. Let’s call him Mr. K.

美国葡萄酒行业堪称顶尖的销售员，最近以美国顶级葡萄酒公司之一董事长的身份结束了自己辉煌的职业生涯。三十多年来，他个人销售了价值数百万美元的葡萄酒，其中许多都是在葡萄酒尚未像今天这样流行起来之前完成的。我们就叫他K先生吧。

According to Mr. K., this was his best sale: In the fifties, Mr. K. was trying to sell wines from an upstate New York winery to one of the most famous and finest establishments in New York City. This legendary restaurant was (and still is) frequented by a cosmopolitan and discriminating clientele, and it served only the best European wines. The restaurant was exclusive and catered to the desires of its patrons.

据K先生说，这是他最成功的一笔交易：五十年代，K先生试图将纽约州北部一家酒庄的葡萄酒卖给纽约市最著名、最高端的餐厅之一。这家传奇餐厅过去（现在）经常光顾着来自世界各地、眼光独到的顾客，而且只供应最优质的欧洲葡萄酒。这家餐厅独具特色，竭力满足顾客的需求。

Mr. K. could not even get an appointment to see the decision maker. For six months the owner refused to see him. Mr. K. learned that the owner regularly ate lunch at the bar at three o’clock. A few days later, Mr. K. simply entered the restaurant and approached the owner while he was at lunch. The following sales call took place.

K先生甚至没能预约到这位决策者。六个月来，这位老板一直拒绝与他见面。K先生得知，这位老板经常在下午三点在酒吧吃午饭。几天后，K先生径直走进餐厅，趁着老板正在吃午饭时上前搭讪。于是，他进行了以下的推销拜访。

M R . K.: Excuse me for interrupting, Mr. Owner. My name is Mr. K. and my purpose is to show you why you should consider putting ABC Wines on your wine list. May I continue?

K先生：抱歉打扰了，老板先生。我叫K先生，我的目的是想告诉您为什么应该考虑将ABC Wines列入您的酒单。我可以继续吗？

O WNER : I am having my lunch.

店主：我正在吃午饭。

M R . K.: Mr. Owner, you meet with your customers every day when they are having lunch. I assure you, I do not wish to be a bother, but like you, meeting customers is also my job. This will take two minutes. May I…?

K先生：老板先生，您每天都会在顾客午餐时与他们见面。我向您保证，我并不想打扰您，但和您一样，接待顾客也是我的工作。这会占用您两分钟的时间。我可以……吗？

O WNER : Two minutes.

主人：两分钟。

M R . K.: Will you please put ABC Wines on your wine list?

MR. K.：请把 ABC Wines 添加到您的酒单上好吗？

O WNER : No.

主人：没有。

M R . K.: Why can’t you?

MR. K.：为什么你不能？

O WNER : The wines taste terrible, and I don’t like them.

店主：这些酒的味道太差了，我不喜欢。

M R . K.: Mr. Owner, I agree with you. The wines do not appeal to everyone. But if I can show you why that doesn’t matter, would you consider them?

MR. K.：老板先生，我同意您的看法。这些酒并非人人都喜欢。但如果我能告诉您为什么这无关紧要，您会考虑吗？

O WNER : I’m listening.

主人：我在听。

M R . K.: Thank you. The reason you should give these wines a try is not because you or I don’t care for the taste, but because thirty-five to forty of your regular customers do like the taste. Mr. Jones and Mr. Smith like ABC Wines. And several times your waiters have been asked if you have those wines. This is a business opportunity worth $200 a week.

K先生：谢谢。您之所以应该尝试一下这些酒，并非因为您或我不喜欢它们的味道，而是因为您店里有三十五到四十位常客喜欢它们的味道。琼斯先生和史密斯先生都喜欢ABC酒庄的葡萄酒。而且，您的服务员也曾多次被问到您是否有这些酒。这是一个每周价值200美元的商机。

Mr. Owner, you should put ABC Wines in here because your customers will order and drink them. Isn’t that reasonable?

老板先生，您应该把ABC葡萄酒放在这里，因为您的顾客会点这些酒，然后喝。这难道不合理吗？

O WNER : I will look into it and decide tomorrow.

业主：我会研究一下，明天再做决定。

M R . K.: That’s fair enough. Thank you.

K先生：好的，谢谢。

The next day, Mr. K. received an order for ten cases of ABC Wines. This was more than a token order, and ABC Wines have been on the wine list ever since. Every major restaurant in New York City soon put Mr. K.’s wines on their wine lists.

第二天，K先生收到了十箱ABC葡萄酒的订单。这不仅仅是一份象征性的订单，从那以后，ABC葡萄酒就一直出现在他们的酒单上。纽约市的每家大餐厅很快就把K先生的葡萄酒列入了他们的酒单。

Case Analysis: Lessons in “Mr. K.”

案例分析：《K先生》中的教训

  1. Mr. K. did his precall homework and determined when and where to find the customer.
    K 先生做好了拜访前的准备工作，确定了何时何地找到客户。
  2. Mr. K. stated clearly and immediately the objective of the sales call, and did so in question form.
    K先生立即清楚的说明了销售拜访的目的，并以提问的形式进行了说明。
  3. Mr. K. was polite, always asking permission to continue. Said “thank you,” “please,” “may I.”
    K先生很有礼貌，每次都要先请求允许才能继续。他会说“谢谢”、“请”、“我可以吗？”
  4. Mr. K. concluded every statement in question form, asking for the owner’s agreement.
    K先生以问题的形式总结了每一句话，并请求业主的同意。
  5. When the owner raised an objection (“I am having my lunch”), Mr. K. reversed the situation. He changed places with the owner by saying, “You meet your customers every day when they are having lunch.” Mr. K.’s message was “If it’s OK for you to interrupt your customer’s lunch, it is OK for me to do the same.”
    当店主提出异议（“我正在吃午饭”）时，K先生扭转了局面。他与店主交换了位置，说道：“你每天都会在顾客吃午饭的时候见到他们。” K先生的意思是：“如果你可以打扰顾客吃午饭，那么我也可以。”
  6. Mr. K. clearly stated the time investment to the owner (two minutes) and got an agreement to that time—the all-important first agreement in the sales cycle.
    K 先生向业主清楚地说明了时间投入（两分钟），并获得了对该时间的同意——这是销售周期中最重要的第一份协议。
  7. In his precall planning, Mr. K. learned about the owner’s customers—the restaurant’s patrons. Mr. K. brought patron research to the owner. Giving a customer new information allows the customer to change his or her mind without losing face.
    在拜访前的计划中，K先生了解了店主的顾客——也就是餐厅的常客。K先生把顾客调查结果带给了店主。向顾客提供新的信息，可以让顾客在不丢面子的情况下改变主意。
  8. Mr. K. used credible third-party testimonials: the comments from the waiters. This is powerful testimony because it can be easily verified.
    K先生使用了可信的第三方证言：服务员的评价。这是强有力的证据，因为它很容易被验证。
  9. Mr. K. asked for the order: “Will you please put ABC Wines on your wine list?” Mr. K. did what some studies indicate that 90 percent of all salespeople don’t do: Mr. K. asked for the order.
    K 先生要求下单：“请把 ABC 酒庄列入您的酒单好吗？”K 先生做了一些研究表明 90% 的销售人员都不会做的事情：K 先生要求下单。
  10. Mr. K. answered the owner’s objection (“no”) with the ingenious “Why can’t you?” The use of the word can’t , as opposed to don’t , or won’t , is a subtle challenge of the owner’s authority and power. “Can’t” implies someone else has the power. This is unacceptable to many customers. If Mr. K. had asked “Why won’t you?” the owner could have comfortably answered with a number of legitimate reasons, such as “We only serve French wines.” To the question “Why don’t you?” the owner could have responded “The wine cellar is full.” But to accede to the question “Why can’t you?” is to say “I’m powerless.”
    Mr. K. thought about and planned the exact wording of this response for weeks.
    K 先生巧妙地用“为什么你不能？”来回答店主的反对意见。使用“不能”这个词，而不是“不”或“不会”，是对店主权威和权力的微妙挑战。“不能”暗示别人有权力。这对许多顾客来说是不可接受的。如果 K 先生问“为什么你不能？”，店主本可以轻松地用一些正当的理由来回答，比如“我们只供应法国葡萄酒”。对于“为什么你不能？”这个问题，店主可以回答“酒窖满了”。但同意“为什么你不能？”这个问题就等于说“我无能为力”。
    K 先生思考并计划了数周的确切措辞。
  11. When the owner objected to the wines’ taste, Mr. K. agreed that it was OK not to like the wines. Mr. K. did not debate. He deflated the rhetoric by agreeing.
    当店主对葡萄酒的味道表示不满时，K先生表示，不喜欢这些酒也没关系。K先生没有争辩，而是以同意的态度平息了争吵。
  12. Mr. K. used an “if I… will you” close (“… if I can show you… would you consider?”). This is good technique because the customer feels the burden is on the salesperson, not on the customer. But if the customer agrees to this proposal, and the salesperson delivers his promise, the customer is committed.
    K先生用了“如果我……你愿意”这样的结尾（“……如果我能带你去看……你会考虑吗？”）。这是一个很好的技巧，因为顾客会觉得负担在销售人员身上，而不是在自己身上。但如果顾客同意这个提议，并且销售人员兑现了他的承诺，那么顾客就做出了承诺。
  13. Mr. K. used a compelling reason for the owner to buy: Thirty-five to forty of the owner’s patrons would order the wine. The owner both satisfies his customers and gets the dollarized benefit of $200 a week in extra sales.
    Mr. K. said, “Give these wines a try.” Mr. K. was posing the purchase as a temporary, changeable, low-risk decision.
    K先生给店主提供了一个令人信服的购买理由：店主的35到40位顾客会点这款酒。店主既满足了顾客的需求，又获得了每周200美元的额外销售额。
    K先生说：“试试这些酒吧。” K先生将这次购买行为描述为一个暂时的、可调整的、低风险的决定。
  14. Mr. K. asked, “Would you consider them?” This is a variation of the killer sales question “Why don’t you give it a try?”
    K先生问道：“你会考虑它们吗？”这是杀手级销售问题“你为什么不试一试？”的变体。
  15. Mr. K. eliminated the all-too-common customer/salesperson give and take. Mr. K. took the focus off what the owner thought and put it on the restaurant patrons and waiters. This is called triangulation. The customer, the salesperson, and the third entity are the points of the triangle. Mr. K. and the owner can refer to the third entity and avoid parrying with each other.
    K先生消除了顾客与销售人员之间常见的互相妥协。K先生将焦点从店主的想法转移到餐厅顾客和服务员身上。这被称为三角关系。顾客、销售人员和第三方是三角形的顶点。K先生和店主可以参考第三方，避免彼此争吵。
  16. Mr. K. used friendly words such as “consider” (twice!), “reasonable,” and “fair.” These words are not inflammatory and encourage mature discourse. The word fair is a strong selling word because it appeals to the customer’s sense of fairness. Being fair leads to more objective, less emotional decision making.
    K先生使用了诸如“考虑”（两次！）、“合理”和“公平”等友好的词语。这些词语不具煽动性，并鼓励成熟的对话。“公平”一词是一个强有力的推销词，因为它能够激发顾客的公平感。公平会让顾客做出更客观、更少情绪化的决策。
  17. Mr. K. received and acknowledged three commitments. The first commitment was the owner’s agreement to two minutes. Mr. K. capitalized on that agreement by immediately asking for the order. Mr. K. acknowledged the second commitment (“I’m listening”) by saying “thank you.” Mr. K. acknowledged the third commitment (“I will look into it”) also by saying “thank you.” Acknowledging and cementing commitments is strong technique.
    The customer realizes he has agreed to something, and if the customer continues, it is a buy signal.
    K先生收到并确认了三项承诺。第一项承诺是店主同意两分钟的回复。K先生充分利用了这项承诺，立即要求下单。K先生通过说“谢谢”来确认第二项承诺（“我正在听着”）。K先生也通过说“谢谢”来确认第三项承诺（“我会考虑一下”）。确认并巩固承诺是一项强大的技巧。
    顾客意识到自己已经同意了某件事，如果顾客继续，则是一个购买信号。
  18. The goal of every sales call is to get a close or a commitment to an action that leads to a close. The customer’s agreement to “look into it” was a commitment to an action that leads to a close. Ergo, a successful sales close.
    每次销售拜访的目标都是促成交易，或者促成交易后采取行动的承诺。客户同意“了解情况”就等于承诺采取行动，最终促成交易。因此，成功的销售成交。
  19. What was Mr. K. actually selling? If he were selling wines, perhaps he might have brought a sample to taste (which would have killed the sale). But Mr. K. wasn’t selling wine. He was selling the dollarized value ($200 a week) the owner would get from featuring the wine. Mr. K. sold money.
    K先生究竟在卖什么？如果他卖的是葡萄酒，或许他会带些样品来品尝（这会影响销量）。但K先生卖的不是葡萄酒。他卖的是店主通过推广葡萄酒所能获得的美元价值（每周200美元）。K先生卖的是钱。
  20. Did Mr. K. break the rule of never making a cold call? Decide for yourself: The owner knew of Mr. K.—after all, he had spurned Mr. K. for six months. Mr. K. knew that a shot on goal is never a bad play. Mr. K. had nothing to lose.
    K先生是不是违反了不主动打电话的规矩？你自己判断吧：老板知道K先生的存在——毕竟，他已经拒绝了K先生六个月了。K先生知道射门永远都是个好主意。K先生也没什么可失去的。

Like every great Rainmaker, Mr. K. was brave and bold, courageous and calm. And like every great Rainmaker… you’ve got to know the rules in order to break them.

如同所有伟大的造雨人一样，K先生勇敢无畏，果敢沉着。正如所有伟大的造雨人一样……你必须了解规则，才能打破规则。

ABOUT THE AUTHOR

关于作者

JEFFREY J. FOX is the founder of Fox & Co., Inc., a premier marketing consulting company, serving more than 100 companies in 100 industries and headquartered in Chester, CT. Fox was previously the vice president of marketing and corporate at Loctite Corporation. A graduate of the Harvard Business School, he was also the director of marketing for the wine division of Pillsbury and held various senior marketing posts at Heublein, Inc., including the director of new products. Fox’s bestselling books have been published in thirty-five languages and have sold more than 1 million copies worldwide.

杰弗里·J·福克斯是福克斯公司（Fox & Co., Inc.）的创始人。该公司是一家领先的营销咨询公司，服务于100个行业的100多家公司，总部位于康涅狄格州切斯特。福克斯曾任乐泰公司（Loctite Corporation）营销和企业副总裁。他毕业于哈佛商学院，曾担任Pillsbury葡萄酒部门的营销总监，并在Heublein公司担任过多个高级营销职位，包括新产品总监。福克斯的畅销书已被翻译成35种语言，全球销量超过100万册。
